Title: AI for Rakyat programme to equip 100,000 youths with AI tools
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: Youths aged between 18 and 30 will be eligible for three months of free access to selected artificial intelligence (AI) tools after completing six modules under the new AI for Rakyat programme.
The Digital Ministry said the programme, which begins tomorrow, would be rolled out in phases through the newly launched Rakyat Digital portal and aims to reach 100,000 Malaysian youths by 2027.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim announced the programme as one of
six immediate measures
for the people during his National Day Eve address at the Putrajaya International Convention Centre (PICC) here today.
"The programme is offered free to eligible Malaysian citizens aged 18 to 30, subject to completion and passing of the prescribed modules.
"The six modules are AI Nation 2030: Madani Approach, Cybersafe for Rakyat, Generative AI, AI Safety, Agentic AI for All and Cloud for Rakyat.
"Participants who successfully complete all six modules will receive three months of free access to selected AI applications and software.
"As an initial offering, eligible participants will receive access to AI tools from local and international technology providers, including YTL AI Labs' IlmuChat, Alibaba's Wonderclip and MuleRun, and Google's Gemini Enterprise," the ministry said in a statement today.
It added that more AI software and tools from other technology companies would be added progressively to broaden the learning experience.
Meanwhile, Digital Ministry secretary-general Datuk Fabian Bigar said the programme aimed to ensure youths not only understood AI technology but also had access to tools that could support learning, creativity and productivity.
"We want to ensure that the benefits of AI can be felt more widely and inclusively, in line with the government's aspiration to build a society that is digitally literate and prepared for the future," he said.
The programme is part of the government's efforts to expand access to AI while building knowledge, skills and confidence among youths to use the technology responsibly.
Rakyat Digital is the national digital learning portal and an initiative of the Digital Ministry led by MyDigital Corporation.
The initiative also supports Malaysia's ambition to develop an inclusive AI nation by 2030 under the MD2030 agenda.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Mat Sabu urges more Bumiputera farmers to go big in commercial agriculture
Article:
SERDANG: Agriculture and Food Security Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Sabu wants more Bumiputera farmers to compete in large-scale agriculture, encouraged by the growing number of young people taking up farming full-time.
"We hope the younger generation will take up agriculture full-time," he said at the launch of new pomelo and sweet potato varieties at Maha  2026 here today.
Mohamad said Bumiputera farmers should compete with communities already established in commercial agriculture.
"We must also compete in this sector because Bumiputeras can do it.
"But it requires full-time commitment.
"I am now seeing more Bumiputeras venturing into agriculture full-time, and that is what impresses me," he said.
He cited one of the recipients at the launch, a former engineer who now operates a 200-acre sweet potato farm in Terengganu, as an example of young Bumiputeras turning to commercial farming.
Meanwhile, the minister launched two new pomelo clones, Melomax 1 and Melomax 2, and the V8 sweet potato variety developed by the Malaysian Agricultural Research and Development Institute (Mardi).
According to Mardi, six recipients received planting materials to support the expansion of the new varieties.
A total of 300 pomelo saplings and 30,000 V8 sweet potato cuttings were distributed for cultivation in Selangor, Kelantan and Sabah.
Maha 2026 is being held at the Malaysia Agro Exposition Park Serdang (Maeps) from Aug 28 to Sept 6.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Langkawi ferry operators urge urgent dredging of Kuala Kedah, Kuala Perlis lanes
Article:
ALOR SETAR: Langkawi ferry operators are appealing to the federal government to expedite dredging works in the shipping lanes at Kuala Kedah and Kuala Perlis, where silt deposits are affecting navigational safety.
Ferry Line Ventures Sdn Bhd operations manager Lieutenant Commander (Retired) Norhafiz Abdul Wahid said increasingly shallow shipping lanes not only increased the risk to passenger ferry operations but could also cause schedule disruptions and travel delays.
"Ferry services are the mainstay of transportation to Langkawi and play an important role in supporting the country's tourism sector.
"Based on previous operational records, passenger ferry services are capable of transporting up to 25,000 tourists a day during peak season," he said in a statement today.
He said if dredging works were not carried out immediately, the situation could affect the smooth operation of ferry services, especially during peak periods, including ahead of the Langkawi International Maritime and Aerospace Exhibition (Lima) next year.
Norhafiz said comprehensive and periodic dredging works were needed to ensure the shipping routes remained safe, while allowing ferry operations to run smoothly and accommodate increased passenger numbers.
In a related development, he said 176 regular ferry trips and 66 additional trips were scheduled between Aug 27 and Sept 6 to accommodate the school holiday and National Day crowds.
He said about 90,000 passengers were expected to travel via the two main routes — Langkawi-Kuala Perlis-Langkawi and Langkawi-Kuala Kedah-Langkawi.
He added that 86,978 tickets had so far been sold through online sales, counters and reservations.
"Visitors are also advised to buy tickets in advance online via the Cuti-Cuti Langkawi application to avoid disappointment," he said.
Norhafiz said the company would ensure a high level of readiness for ferry operations throughout the school holiday season and National Day.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Anwar: Malaysia's economic strength shines amid geopolitical uncertainty
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: Malaysia's six per cent gross domestic product (GDP) growth in the second quarter of this year marks a new chapter in the country's journey towards greater progress and prosperity.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the achievement was particularly encouraging as it came amid an uncertain geopolitical environment, especially the ongoing conflict in the Middle East.
"Imagine this, no one expected such growth based on the projections. No one.
"Not the World Bank, not the International Monetary Fund (IMF). No one projected the strength of our economy.
"But in the second quarter of 2026, Malaysia's GDP grew by six per cent," he said during his National Day Eve address at the Putrajaya International Convention Centre (PICC) here today.
Present were Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi, Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil, National Unity Minister Datuk Aaron Ago Dagang and Chief Secretary to the Government Tan Sri Shamsul Azri Abu Bakar.
Anwar said the positive achievement was the result of efforts and leadership built up since independence and was not achieved overnight.
"Approved investments and total trade reached their highest levels in history since 1957 and 1963. Malaysia's competitiveness rose to 15th place this year. The ringgit emerged as Asia's best-performing currency in 2025.
"The government and my cabinet colleagues chose the difficult path, strengthening the country's fundamentals, improving governance and restoring fiscal discipline.
"Closing avenues for leakages, expediting approvals and building confidence in Malaysia," he said.
Meanwhile, Anwar said Malaysia's ability to remain peaceful and united despite its racial, religious and cultural diversity continued to be one of the country's greatest strengths.
"We have one homeland, Malaysia. We have inherited the history of a nation, and we are responsible for ensuring a glorious future," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Anwar: Economic growth benefits must be shared fairly among Malaysians
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: The government must ensure that the benefits of Malaysia's economic growth are shared fairly among all segments of society, regardless of race, religion, region or background, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said.
He said the Madani government faced the challenge of balancing the needs of different groups, including the M40 and B40, Malay and Bumiputera communities, minorities, Sabah and Sarawak, as well as youths, women, persons with disabilities and workers in various sectors.
"How do we ensure the T20 continue to have confidence to invest? How do we protect the M40 and B40?
"How do we address the problems faced by Malays and Bumiputera, particularly those who are still feeling marginalised in certain areas?
"And what about the aspirations of the Chinese, Indians, Orang Asli, Sabah and Sarawak?" he said in his National Day Eve address at the Putrajaya International Convention Centre here today.
Anwar also said the government must take into account the needs of young people, workers, women, farmers, fishermen, hawkers and gig workers.
He said these challenges reflected the government's responsibility to ensure that development and prosperity were enjoyed by the people as a whole.
The finance minister acknowledged that Malaysians continued to face pressure from the rising cost of living despite the country's economic progress.
He said the government had increased allocations for Sumbangan Tunai Rahmah (STR) and Sumbangan Asas Rahmah (SARA) to RM15 billion this year, the highest in the programmes' history.
"Does this satisfy me? No. Does this reduce the hardship caused by the cost of living? Not yet. We acknowledge that continuous measures must be taken," he said.
Anwar said the government had also introduced measures benefiting the M40, including a two-percentage-point reduction in income tax rates from 2023, which he said had resulted in RM1 billion in foregone revenue.
He said the government had also increased early schooling assistance to RM150 per pupil, regardless of family background.
On electricity subsidies, Anwar said the targeted subsidy programme had benefited 85 per cent of users, with the government spending about RM4 billion.
He said the government had also continued to strengthen grassroots programmes such as Kampung Angkat Madani, Sekolah Angkat Madani and Sejati Madani.
Anwar stressed that the government did not consider its work complete, acknowledging that many Malaysians were still struggling with living costs while small and medium-sized businesses continued to face cost pressures.
He said concerns also remained over infrastructure and access to healthcare, with Malaysians in various parts of the country still facing difficulties and long waits at hospitals and clinics.
"Every citizen, Malay, Iban, Kadazan, Orang Asli, Chinese or Indian, is a Malaysian citizen who must be given due attention and protection," he said.
Anwar said the government's priority was to strengthen unity while ensuring that the country's economic progress translated into better opportunities and living conditions for all Malaysians.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Kelantan Umno leaders to attend Pas muktamar, says Takiyuddin
Article:
KOTA BARU: Umno secretary-general and Kelantan Umno leaders, including the state liaison chairman and division chiefs, have confirmed their attendance at the Pas muktamar.
Pas and Perikatan Nasional (PN) secretary-general Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan said invitations had also been extended to other Umno leaders, including the heads of the party's Youth and Wanita wings.
"The confirmed attendees are the Umno secretary-general and Umno leaders in Kelantan, including the state liaison chairman and division chiefs.
"Umno Youth chief Datuk Dr Muhamad Akmal Saleh will attend the Youth muktamar.
"I understand that the Wanita Umno chief Datuk Seri Dr Noraini Ahmad has also been invited. I am not sure whether she will attend, but there will be a representative from Wanita Umno," he said when met after visiting the muktamar venue here today.
He said PN would also invite leaders from its component parties, including Parti Wawasan Rakyat, Gerakan and Parti Makkal Sakti Malaysia (MIPP).
Non-governmental organisations (NGOs) and foreign guests would also be invited to the muktamar, he said.
"Among them are Islamic movements from Bangladesh, Pakistan, Türkiye, Indonesia and Thailand, as well as several other countries," he said.
On reports that Umno had invited Pas to its upcoming general assembly, Takiyuddin said Pas had yet to receive an official invitation.
"We have been told about it, but we have not received the invitation yet.
"If we receive the invitation, I am confident that Pas will send a representative there.
"So far, there is no official invitation. Personally, I have not received one, and my office in Kuala Lumpur has also not informed me of receiving it.
"However, verbally, there have been reports through the media," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Communications Ministry to step up efforts to spread information on government assistance
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: The Communications Ministry will step up efforts to ensure Malaysians are better informed about government assistance, initiatives and achievements.
Its minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said the ministry would help communicate the various measures announced by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, including financial assistance and fuel subsidies, and ensure the information reached the public effectively.
"This is something we will help communicate to the public, so that the message from the Prime Minister on the government's efforts, achievements and assistance provided reaches Malaysians," he told reporters here today after Anwar's National Day Eve address at the Putrajaya International Convention Centre.
Fahmi said the government had allocated RM15 billion for Sumbangan Tunai Rahmah (STR) this year, while RM40 billion had been set aside for RON95 and diesel subsidies under the Budi Madani programmes.
"The figures for the assistance provided by the government are actually very large," he said.
He said the STR allocation was significantly higher than the amount previously provided under earlier assistance schemes, including Bantuan Rakyat 1Malaysia.
Earlier, Anwar announced that the monthly Budi Madani RON95 (BUDI95) subsidised petrol quota would be restored to 300 litres, while the monthly diesel allocation for eligible four-wheel-drive and pickup owners would be increased to 400 litres, effective Sept 1.
Fahmi said his ministry would also communicate other measures announced during the address, including the decision to raise the e-Invoice exemption threshold from RM1 million to RM3 million.
The move is expected to benefit more than 1.1 million businesses.
The government also increased the allocation for digital healthcare initiatives from RM650 million to RM1 billion to accelerate digital access, including public Wi-Fi at government clinics and hospitals and the expansion of electronic medical records.
Meanwhile, 100,000 Malaysians aged between 18 and 30 will have the opportunity to receive three months' free subscriptions to three AI applications after completing the AI Untuk Rakyat programme.
Fahmi said further details on the AI initiative would be provided by the Digital Ministry.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Firefighter's brother to join Smart mission in Nepal to search for missing sibling
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: The brother of Malaysian firefighter Mohd Fakhrul Munir, who remains uncontactable in Nepal, will join the Malaysian Special Disaster Assistance and Rescue Team (Smart) mission to the country following the disaster in Rasuwa.
Mohd Saiful Munir Mohd Isa, 46, said he would join the rescue mission as a member of the team while also hoping to obtain news on the whereabouts and condition of his 44-year-old younger brother, known as 'Loe'.
He said he would make full use of the opportunity to enter Nepal to contribute his expertise to the rescue efforts while continuing to seek information on his brother.
"We will try our best, InsyaAllah. I also thank the government for providing us with this opportunity. I am a rescuer myself, but more importantly, I have a brother there," he told reporters after attending a meeting with Wisma Putra representatives here today.
Saiful said he hoped his presence in Nepal would enable him to contribute to the rescue mission while providing some relief to the family, which is still waiting for news of Mohd Fakhrul.
Yesterday, Saiful said he and his family remained positive and hoped Fakhrul and his friends were safe after losing contact with them following the disaster in Rasuwa.
He said the family still hoped the loss of contact was caused by communication disruptions following the disaster and that Fakhrul and his friends were safe.
Earlier today, family members of Malaysians who remain uncontactable following flash floods and landslides in Nepal began arriving at Wisma Putra here from 10am.
The meeting, held at 11am, allowed the families to receive briefings from the Foreign Ministry and the National Security Council on the status of their family members and search efforts in the disaster-hit areas.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Family unaware three children remained inside house during fire
Article:
KOTA KINABALU: The family of three children who were killed in a fire at Kampung Lok Buta, Numbak, early today did not realise that they were still in the house when the incident occurred.
M Nasir Jalani, 68, the grandfather of the three victims, said he woke up after hearing one of his children screaming that their neighbour's house was on fire.
"Upon learning that my house could not be saved, I ran out. I ran back into the house, but the children were not there.
"If I had known they were in the room, perhaps I could have saved them," he said when met at the scene today.
Also present at the scene was Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Sabah and Sarawak) Datuk Mustapha Sakmud, who is also the Sepanggar member of Parliament.
M Nasir said he had invited his three grandchildren to stay at his house a few days ago to celebrate the wedding of one of his children, but never expected the tragedy to occur.
He said the family only realised that the three children were missing after they had reached a safe area.
More than 200 houses were destroyed, while three children, including two siblings, lost their lives in the early morning fire.
The victims were identified as Nana Abdullah, 4, her brother Mohd Asrul Abdullah, 6, and their cousin Nurfarahdilah Mohd Tajihah, 8.
Meanwhile, Roslani Ladin, 65, said he managed to rescue more than 10 members of his family by using a boat to take them to a relative's house not far from the scene.
Roslani, who is also a fisherman, said he made several trips to move his family to safety as the fire had yet to spread to his house at the time, although the house was eventually destroyed in the blaze.
"We have lived here for over 20 years. There had been fires before, but not here.
"This is the first time it has happened in Kampung Lok Buta," he said, adding that he was now staying temporarily at one of his children's homes.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Orangutan rescued from fire zone in Indonesia's Borneo, battles respiratory illness
Article:
KETAPANG, Indonesia:  On Sunday morning, Jais, a farmer in Ketapang, West Kalimantan on Borneo island - the province hardest-hit by raging forest fires - was en route to his farm when he found an orangutan writhing on the ground in a weak state on a palm-oil plantation near the fire site.
"It was very weak, then I gave it water," said Jais, who only goes by one name.
Indonesia has intensified efforts to contain haze from forest and land fires across six provinces in Borneo and Sumatra islands after smoke triggered respiratory illnesses and forced thousands of schools to move classes online, including in neighbouring Malaysia.
Wildfires burned at least 202,010 hectares (499,177.58 acres) of land from January to July, according to Indonesia's Forestry Ministry, increasing from 107,465 burned hectares from January to June.
After finding the orangutan, Jais and other residents immediately called for help.
Some two hours later, a wildlife foundation - Yayasan Inisiasi Alam Rehabilitasi Indonesia - arrived with a veterinarian to provide the animal with treatment. It had fainted by then.
The orangutan was then named Sampurna, after the village where it was found.
Foundation CEO Karmele Llano Sanchez said the orangutan fainted because it did not get enough oxygen.
"The orangutan got hypoxia because of the very thick smoke in the area," Sanchez told Reuters.
Komara, the veterinarian, said the orangutan did not have any severe burn-related injuries. But it had breathing problems and had vomited.
"We suspected it was suffering from an acute respiratory infection," he said, adding that the orangutan is around 20 years old.
At the palm-oil plantation, the orangutan lay on a net, appearing weak with its eyes closed. The veterinarian gave the orangutan oxygen through small tubes placed in its nose.
Sampurna received fluids through an intravenous drip, with a makeshift infusion bag hanging from a palm-oil frond.
The animal will be moved to a rehabilitation center to get more treatment, she said. It will be released back into the wild once it recovers, said Komara, adding that they have rescued seven orangutans due to fires so far.
Sanchez warned that the government must not only focus on containing fires, but prepare for the long-term effects on public health, forests and wildlife. — REUTERS
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Anwar unveils six measures to ease cost-of-living pressures in National Day Eve address
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has announced six immediate measures to ease cost-of-living pressures, support businesses and strengthen public services ahead of the tabling of 2027 Budget in October.
Anwar said the government decided to introduce the measures now instead of waiting for the Budget as Malaysians and businesses were facing immediate challenges.
"Cost-of-living pressures cannot wait until October. Businesses need to grow now and cannot wait until October,"he said during his National Day Eve address at the Putrajaya International Convention Centre  here today.
Apart from increasing the monthly subsidised RON95 entitlement under Budi95 from 200 to 300 litres, the measures include a higher school maintenance allocation, expanded access to artificial intelligence tools for youths, greater digitalisation of public healthcare, a higher e-Invoice exemption threshold and additional microfinancing for small traders.
The government will increase the 2025 maintenance allocation for all types of schools by 50 per cent, from RM1 billion to RM1.5 billion.
Anwar said the additional allocation would cover national schools, Chinese and Tamil vernacular schools, religious schools, tahfiz institutions, pondok schools and special education facilities.
He said the Education Ministry would begin visiting districts from next month to assess applications for infrastructure repairs, without having to wait until next year.
Anwar also announced that the AI for Rakyat programme would be expanded to Malaysians aged between 18 and 30.
"100,000 youths who completed the prescribed modules would receive free three-month subscriptions to leading AI applications."
The programme will provide access to AI tools and services including ChatGPT, Gemini Enterprise, Wondershare and Meituan.
He also said the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) would allocate RM1 billion to strengthen digital capabilities in the public healthcare sector.
"The funding will include the implementation of electronic medical records and internet connectivity at 150 hospitals and more than 2,000 public health clinics."
Anwar said the initiative was aimed at speeding up treatment and reducing long waiting times for patients.
The finance minister also announced that the annual sales threshold for e-Invoice exemption would be raised from RM1 million to RM3 million.
This means businesses with annual sales of up to RM3 million will not be required to implement e-Invoicing.
Anwar said the move would provide relief to micro, small and medium enterprises.
The government will also increase microfinancing facilities for small traders by RM1 billion, bringing total funding for 2025 from RM5 billion to RM6 billion.
A RM200 million Geran Sejahtera Madani will also be introduced to assist hawkers, small traders, night-market traders and women running home-based businesses.
Anwar said the measures reflected the government's principle that economic growth should ultimately benefit the people.
Present were Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi, Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil, National Unity Minister Datuk Aaron Ago Dagang and Chief Secretary to the Government Tan Sri Shamsul Azri Abu Bakar.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Next of kin of missing Malaysians in Nepal told to prepare for DNA tests
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: The next of kin of Malaysians who have yet to be traced following flash floods and landslides in Nepal have been asked to prepare to undergo deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) tests to assist in the identification process.
Sivakumar Kalimuthu, 57, who is still awaiting news of his wife, Kalai Mathe Karuppaiah, 57, said he and his family were informed of the need to undergo the test during a briefing session with the Foreign Ministry at Wisma Putra today.
"The police will contact us for the DNA test, and I need to gather my three children for it," he told reporters.
He said the DNA test was among the preparations being made following the discovery of several unidentified bodies in the disaster area, which had to be buried immediately due to a lack of suitable storage facilities.
He said his three children are currently in Singapore, Langkawi and Selangor, and all of them are still grieving but continue to hope that their mother will be found safe.
Recalling his last communication with his wife, a housewife, Sivakumar said he received a call from Kalai Mathe at about 11am last Tuesday.
"My wife informed me that she and a group of 17 Malaysian tourists wanted to travel to Kailash to pray, but after that there was no further communication," he said.
Sivakumar said he continued to pray for his wife's safety and hoped to bring her home.
Earlier, a closed-door briefing by the Foreign Ministry informed the next of kin of Malaysians who have yet to be traced that they would be encouraged to undergo DNA tests at the police contingent headquarters from tomorrow, following official notification.
The samples will be used for cross-referencing to identify victims of the incident in Chitwan, Nepal.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: C4 calls for audit department review after RM4.8bil TH discrepancy
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: An anti-graft watchdog has called for a review of the National Audit Department after a RM4.8 billion discrepancy emerged between the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report on Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH) and the department's report on the fund's finances.
Centre to Combat Corruption and Cronyism (C4) head of research and policy advocacy Arief Hamizan said the discrepancy raised questions over whether financial mismanagement in other statutory bodies may have gone undetected despite being subjected to standard accounting practices, according to FMT.
"It calls into question how many cases of financial mismanagement in other statutory bodies have yet to be uncovered," he said.
Arief said an urgent review of the department's audit practices and governance structure was needed to ensure its audits accurately reflected the financial position of statutory bodies.
He also called for institutional reforms to prevent financial mismanagement, including a ban on political appointments to statutory bodies and government-linked companies.
He said the conflicting findings highlighted weaknesses in the National Audit Department's role as an oversight institution, particularly in ensuring transparency in the use of public funds.
Stronger oversight was needed to prevent statutory bodies from being abused for personal or political gain, he said.
The RCI found that TH should have reported a net loss of RM1.4 billion for the 2017 financial year, instead of the RM3.4 billion profit declared, if Malaysian Financial Reporting Standards had been fully adhered to.
The commission identified the sources of the discrepancy as changes to the fund's impairment policies, the use of a Realisable Asset Value approach based on management estimates rather than independent professional valuations, and unrecorded losses on investments in subsidiaries and associate companies.
The RCI's findings were corroborated by a financial review conducted by PwC, which found that TH had not carried out the necessary impairment assessments on its investments and had been running an asset-liability deficit since 2014.
The National Audit Department, however, issued a clean audit opinion on the fund's 2017 accounts under the accounting standards in force at the time.
Former auditor-general
Tan Sri Dr Madinah Mohamad
said the discrepancy mainly involved how asset impairments and investments were recognised and valued, and that she and her team found no evidence of theft or misappropriation during their audit.
She said comparing the two reports was akin to comparing "apples and oranges", given their differing purposes, terms of reference and methodologies.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Two-hectare forested area in Taman Bukit Serdang catches fire
Article:
SERDANG: A two-hectare forested area in Taman Bukit Serdang caught fire today, with firefighters managing to contain the blaze.
Selangor Fire and Rescue Department assistant director of operations Ashrul Riezal Asbar said the fire was brought under control after firebreaks were established to prevent it from spreading to nearby areas.
He said the department received a distress call at 1.51pm, with fire engines arriving at the scene at 2.16pm.
"The fire involved secondary hill forest, lalang-covered areas and small patches of forest.
"Firebreaks were established to ensure the fire did not spread to other areas.
"As of 3.15pm, about 80 per cent of the fire had been put out, while firefighters were working to tackle the remaining 20 per cent," he said in a statement.
Ashrul said the fire was reported in an area near 30, Jalan BS 7/14, Taman Bukit Serdang.
"The operation involved a total of 16 personnel from the Puchong Fire and Rescue Station, with assistance from the Sungai Besi Fire and Rescue Station and the Seri Serdang Volunteer Fire Brigade.
"Two Fire Rescue Tenders and an Emergency Medical Rescue Services vehicle were also deployed," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: [UPDATED] Anwar: Billions seized from illegal activities to fund education, healthcare
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: Billions of ringgit seized from the proceeds of illegal activities through legal proceedings and court decisions will be channelled back to the people, particularly for education and healthcare, said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.
Anwar said the move was part of the government's commitment to ensuring recovered proceeds from wrongdoing ultimately benefited the public.
"Today I declare that all funds seized from the proceeds of illegal activities through legal processes and decisions by the judiciary, amounting to billions of ringgit, will be returned, especially for the people's education and healthcare," he said during his National Day Eve address at the Putrajaya International Convention Centre (PICC) here today.
Present were Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi, Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil, National Unity Minister Datuk Aaron Ago Dagang and Chief Secretary to the Government Tan Sri Shamsul Azri Abu Bakar.
Anwar, who is also finance minister, said economic growth must translate into tangible benefits for the people, while wealth obtained through unlawful activities should not remain in the hands of those responsible.
He also stressed that there should be no impunity for companies or individuals involved in corruption, abuse of power or other wrongdoing that resulted in billions of ringgit in losses.
Anwar said the government's approach was based on the principle that the country's economic growth and recovered assets should ultimately benefit the people.
The announcement came as Anwar outlined a series of immediate measures aimed at easing cost-of-living pressures, supporting businesses and strengthening public services ahead of the tabling of the 2027 Budget.
He said the government would continue working with enforcement agencies and relevant institutions to ensure action was taken through proper legal processes.
Anwar said the meaning of independence would be diminished if the country's wealth was not returned to the people or if sections of society were left behind.
"What is the meaning of independence if the country's wealth is not returned to the people?
"What is the meaning of independence if there are children in remote and marginalised communities who do not have the opportunity to enjoy the prosperity enjoyed by others?" he said.
He said every Malaysian, regardless of ethnic background, deserved appropriate attention and support.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: [UPDATED] Budi95 quota restored to 300 litres, diesel allocation raised from Sept 1[WATCH]
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: The government will restore the monthly Budi Madani RON95 (Budi95) subsidised petrol quota from 200 to 300 litres, benefiting more than 16 million users, effective Sept 1.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the move was among six immediate measures introduced to ease cost-of-living pressures and support Malaysians ahead of the 2027 Budget tabling in Oct.
He said the government decided to act immediately instead of asking the people to wait for the Budget, as the pressures facing households and businesses could not be postponed.
"I had to find a way and take a step that would provide relief to the people," he said during his National Day Eve address at the Putrajaya International Convention Centre (PICC) here today.
Anwar said the revised entitlement meant more than 16 million users would be able to purchase up to 300 litres of subsidised RON95 each month.
He also announced that more than 500,000 eligible owners of diesel vehicles, including four-wheel-drive vehicles and pick-ups, would receive Budi Diesel assistance of up to 400 litres a month.
The Budi95 quota was previously set at 300 litres a month before being temporarily reduced to 200 litres from April 1.
The price of RON95 petrol under the programme remains at RM1.99 per litre.
Previously, in June, the government set the basic Budi Diesel allocation at 200 litres a month, with subsidised diesel priced at RM2.10 per litre.
Finance Minister II Datuk Seri Amir Hamzah Azizan said eligible diesel users with qualifying four-wheel-drive vehicles and pick-up trucks could apply for an additional 100 litres, bringing their monthly entitlement to up to 300 litres.
The nationwide implementation of the subsidised diesel pricing mechanism is carried out through a MyKad-based system, similar to Budi95.
Under the latest announcement, the maximum Budi Diesel entitlement will be increased further to 400 litres a month for eligible users.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 13 hotspots detected in Malaysia as Indonesian fires worsen haze
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Thirteen hotspots were detected across Malaysia on Aug 29, as nearly 1,200 hotspots burned in Kalimantan and smoke from Indonesian fires continued to worsen haze conditions across the region.
In a statement, Department of Environment (DOE) deputy director-general (Development) Azuri Azizah Saedon said data from the NOAA-20 satellite, analysed by the Asean Specialised Meteorological Centre (ASMC) in Singapore, detected 1,180 hotspots in Kalimantan and 18 in Sumatra.
The data also showed 13 hotspots in Malaysia — two in Perak, two in Sabah and nine in Sarawak.
She said the ASMC's regional haze map for Aug 29 showed dry weather conditions prevailing across most of the southern Asean region, except northern Sumatra and Peninsular Malaysia, which received some rainfall.
Widespread hotspots were recorded in Kalimantan, while isolated hotspots were detected in Sulawesi, southern and central Sumatra, central Sarawak and East Java.
Azuri said moderate to dense transboundary smoke haze had been detected in West Kalimantan and was moving north into western Sarawak.
Moderate to dense haze was also observed across most of Kalimantan, central Sarawak, and central and southern Sumatra.
In response to the increasing hotspot activity and worsening haze in the southern Asean region, the ASMC Secretariat activated Alert Level 3 for southern Asean effective Aug 27, in accordance with the Asean Standard Operating Procedure for Monitoring, Assessment, and Joint Emergency Response (SOP MAJER).
Earlier today, air quality across Malaysia was reported to have
worsened significantly overnight
as transboundary haze from Indonesia intensified as of 8.18am. Read the earlier report
Data from the DOE's Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS) showed Sarawak recorded the worst readings in the country.
Of the 68 stations monitored nationwide, none recorded good air quality, with 47 recording moderate readings and 20 recording readings ranging from unhealthy to hazardous.

Title: Technician held for throwing stone at vehicle after road dispute on highway [WATCH]
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A man in his 30s was arrested by police after allegedly throwing a stone at a vehicle on the Kuala Lumpur-Seremban Expressway in Sungai Besi yesterday.
Cheras district police chief Assistant Commissioner Mohd Rosdi Daud said the suspect, who works as a technician, was arrested by the roadside along Jalan Suasa 3, Sungai Besi, about 1.15am today.
He said the suspect was believed to have thrown a stone at the vehicle, causing its rear windscreen to shatter in the incident, which took place about 2pm yesterday.
"The motive was believed to stem from a road dispute, in which the suspect was dissatisfied and claimed that the complainant's vehicle had cut into his path," he said in a statement today.
Rosdi said the police had obtained a three-day remand order from the magistrate's court against the suspect, starting today until Sept 1, to assist in investigations.
He said the case was being investigated under Section 427 of the Penal Code for mischief causing damage.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Middle East conflict weighs on Wasco earnings outlook
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Research firms have lowered their earnings forecast for Wasco Bhd, citing supply chain disruptions arising from the ongoing conflict in the Middle East that are expected to weigh on the company's operations.
RHB Research trimmed its earnings forecasts for the company by 53 per cent, 37 per cent and 17 per cent for financial year 2026 (FY26), FY27 and FY28, respectively, to reflect weaker near-term project execution.
The lower earnings estimates were also made due to a more conservative assumption for orderbook replenishment and project execution amid delays in investment decisions.
The firm noted that Wasco's orderbook stood at RM2.5 billion as at the second quarter of 2026 (Q2 FY26), reflecting continued replenishment from newly secured projects.
"We expect pipeline coating activities to gain traction only in 2H FY26 as several projects remain deferred in the near term.
"In addition, a potential easing in geopolitical tensions could support the resumption of deferred energy infrastructure projects and repair activities, potentially increasing demand for pipeline coating and engineering services," it added.
RHB Research said that Wasco's core earnings of RM23.8 million for 1H FY26 came below expectations at 24 per cent of the firm's estimates and accounted for 27 per cent of the consensus' forecast.
The negative variance was largely due to weaker-than-expected contributions from both the energy services and renewable segments.
"Nevertheless, we remain constructive as we view the weakness as execution-related, while a replenishing orderbook, improving margins, and potential resumption of deferred projects should support earnings recovery," it added.
RHB Research kept its "Buy" call on Wasco with a lower target price of RM1.15.
Hong Leong Investment Bank Bhd (HLIB) lowered its earnings forecasts for Wasco by 21.6 per cent and 13.19 per cent for FY26 and FY27, respectively, to reflect weaker contributions from the Energy Services division following the ongoing Middle East operational disruptions.
The firm expects the disruption to spill over into Q1 FY27.
HLIB said that Wasco started 1H FY26 on a softer footing, mainly due to disruptions on the two pipeline projects in Qatar arising from shortages of iron ore raw materials, with the affected projects accounting for 20 per cent of its revenue.
"Nevertheless, other projects remain under execution, with the affected orderbook delayed rather than cancelled. Wasco's order book remains healthy at RM2.5 billion as of Q2 FY26, alongside an RM11 billion tender book, evenly split between engineering and pipeline opportunities.
"Looking beyond the nearterm disruptions, we believe Wasco remains well-positioned to benefit from rising energy security-driven capex, supported by demand for pipeline coating, engineering works, FPSO developments and broader energy infrastructure expansion across key markets such as Qatar and Pengerang," it said.
HLIB kept its "Buy" call on the stock with a lower target price of RM1.14.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: SunCon poised to surpass RM8 billion contract wins, says HLIB
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Sunway Construction Group Bhd (SunCon) is likely to win more than RM8 billion in new contracts for financial year 2026 (FY26), with year-to-date wins already totalling RM6.9 billion, said Hong Leong Investment Bank Bhd (HLIB).
The research house said the latest wins have lifted SunCon's unbilled order book to a record RM10.5 billion as at June 2026, about twice the amount of its FY25 revenue.
It added that SunCon's tenderbook remains sizable at RM14.2 billion, largely comprising data centre projects with more than 700 megawatts (MW) of capacity, providing robust visibility for orderbook replenishment over the near-to-medium term.
"With several months left in the year, we see upside risk to our fairly conservative FY26 contract win assumption of RM8 billion," it said in a note.
HLIB added that SunCon could also benefit from its parent company Sunway Bhd's project pipeline, including rapid transit system transport-oriented development works and Seremban hospital works, in our view," it added.
Meanwhile, HLIB said that SunCon's core earnings of RM218 million for the first half of FY26 came in within the firm's and consensus' expectations at 53 per cent and 51 per cent, respectively.
HLIB kept its "Buy" call on the stock with an unchanged target price of RM9.10 based on 23 times its FY27 earnings per share.
"In our view, SunCon's premium valuation is justified given its strong alpha to the data centre theme, robust execution capabilities with solid margin delivery and superior ROEs alongside an attractive dividend yield of six per cent," it said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: OCK set for earnings lift from RM500mil diigital pipeline
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: OCK Group Bhd is likely to see stronger earnings going forward on the back of its growing digital infrastructure tenderbook, said RHB Research.
The research firm said that OCK is shifting its focus away from the legacy site contracting business, where growth appears to be levelling off.
In addition to broadband and connectivity jobs for various university campuses, military camps, and related points of presence and fibreisation deals, the firm said that OCK has also made good inroads into smart city projects, which is supportive of the digital infrastructure tender book of RM500 million.
"We expect some of these projects to translate into actual wins going forward, which could materially lift margins and earnings in the medium term.
"On its towerco business, we see management scaling up its regional portfolio of sites via inorganic acquisitions, ahead of a potential initial public offering down the road," it said.
HLIB added that OCK's results for the fourth quarter and financial year 2026 were broadly in line with a bumped RM9.5 million dividend income booked from its solar asset investment during the quarter.
OCK posted its highest-ever quarterly results for the fourth quarter ended June 30, 2026 (Q4 FY26), driven by stronger telecommunications, artificial intelligence and data centre contributions.
Revenue rose 24.2 per cent year-on-year (YoY) to RM229 million from RM184.4 million, while pre-tax profit surged 135.9 per cent to RM36.1 million from RM15.3 million.
Net profit jumped 218.1 per cent to RM23.6 million from RM7.4 million, while profit after tax attributable to minority interests soared 384.6 per cent to RM19.4 million from RM4 million.
HLIB maintained its "Buy" call on the stock with a target price of 74 sen.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Chow: Merdeka is a responsibility to preserve peace, harmony
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: Penang will continue supporting the Madani Government's agenda while ensuring the state's development benefits all communities, said Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow.
Chow said Penang's economic progress must go hand in hand with efforts to strengthen social harmony and improve the people's quality of life.
In his National Day message issued today, Chow said Malaysia's 69 years of independence should serve as a reminder that freedom was an 'amanah' (trust) that must be safeguarded.
"Malaysia's independence is not merely about remembering the moment of freedom, but also reminding ourselves that it is an 'amanah' that must be continuously preserved to ensure peace, defend harmony and ensure Malaysia continues to move forward," he said.
Chow said the country's progress should not be measured solely through economic figures, but also translated into better living conditions for the people.
This included quality employment opportunities, affordable housing, a more manageable cost of living, and a safe and sustainable environment for families.
He said Penang would remain committed to the Malaysia Madani agenda, particularly in ensuring the state's development continued without neglecting the people's socioeconomic wellbeing.
"Penang may be small in size, but its contribution to Malaysia is significant," he added, citing the state's roles in manufacturing and technology, education, tourism and innovation.
Chow said Penang's diverse population remained one of its greatest strengths and urged the people to continue respecting differences in race, religion, culture and background.
"Progress will have no meaning without harmony in society. Penang was built by people of various races, religions, cultures and backgrounds. This diversity is our strength," he stressed.
He said the state would continue working towards the Penang2030 vision while strengthening development and ensuring its benefits were enjoyed by all residents.
"Our resolve is clear — to support the Malaysia Madani agenda, strengthen Penang's development and ensure the benefits of progress are enjoyed by all the people," he said.
Chow also urged Penangites to remain united despite their differences, saying the state's future depended on collective efforts to preserve harmony.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Haze: Experts urge public to monitor API, take health precautions
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The public should monitor daily Air Pollutant Index (API) readings and take appropriate precautions to reduce health risks during the current haze, according to health experts.
Universiti Sultan Zainal Abidin (UniSZA) Faculty of Health Sciences lecturer Dr Anas Ahmad Jamhari said people should check the daily API readings issued by the Department of Environment (DOE) before engaging in outdoor activities, particularly when readings exceed 100.
He said those who had to leave home for essential purposes should wear an N95 mask correctly and ensure a proper seal to filter fine PM2.5 particles.
"For those who need to work outdoors for long periods, an N95 mask is the most suitable, provided it is worn correctly and fits tightly.
However, its effectiveness is reduced if it is loose, frequently removed, wet, damaged or worn with a beard that affects the seal.
"Wearing a mask is also less effective for children when the size is unsuitable and does not provide a proper seal," he told Bernama recently.
Anas also advised the public to avoid strenuous outdoor activities such as running, cycling and sports, as exercise increases the breathing rate and causes more air to be inhaled, allowing more fine particles to enter the respiratory tract.
"What I see is that people are still engaging in outdoor activities even when the API has been categorised as unhealthy.
This increases the risk of both acute and chronic health effects," he said.
At home, he advised keeping doors and windows closed and reducing indoor sources of pollution, including cigarette and vape smoke, burning incense or candles, and cooking activities that produce large amounts of smoke
"When using air-conditioning in a vehicle, make sure the system is set to recirculate indoor air rather than draw in air from outside," he said, adding that open burning should be stopped immediately.
From a toxicology perspective, Anas said haze was not merely smoke that reduced visibility but contained a mixture of particles and chemicals.
Fine PM2.5 particles were particularly concerning because their small size allows them to penetrate deep into the lungs.
When these particles settle in the respiratory system, they can trigger oxidative stress, which may lead to inflammation, cell damage and impaired respiratory function.
Meanwhile, public health medicine specialist Datuk Dr Zainal Ariffin Omar said people should also take temperature and humidity into account during haze episodes, in addition to API readings.
He advised the public to ensure adequate water intake, as the combination of haze and high temperatures could increase the risk of heatstroke and dehydration.
"During an El Niño phenomenon with hot weather, we face a double risk from both haze and heatstroke.
Therefore, a comprehensive approach should address both threats rather than focusing solely on API readings," he said.
He said treating haze as a seasonal phenomenon could cause people to continue their normal routines, potentially reducing their preparedness for subsequent episodes.
Public awareness should therefore be strengthened continuously through simple and easy-to-understand information so that people do not wait until API readings reach higher levels before taking action.
Yesterday, the Health Ministry (MOH) reported that asthma cases at sentinel facilities had increased more than eightfold to 1,811 cases in Epidemiological Week 34, from 219 cases the previous week.
Conjunctivitis cases also rose from 146 to 720 during the same period. — BERNAMA

Title: 15 friends build Twin Towers replica from 2,000 bottles for National Day
Article:
KOTA BARU: A dream of seeing the Petronas Twin Towers up close has taken an unexpected turn, inspiring 15 friends to build a six-metre-high replica from more than 2,000 discarded plastic bottles.
The towering structure, built in front of their homes in Kampung Machang Limbat, took the group several days to complete, with work beginning last Thursday and finishing yesterday.
Mohamad Zul Ikwan Azhar, 28, said the project was inspired by his dream of seeing the KLCC towers up close.
"I have always dreamed of seeing the Petronas Twin Towers in person, so we decided to build one here in our village as our own way of celebrating Merdeka," he said.
Zul Ikwan said the group spent about RM3,000 on the project, while the plastic bottles used to construct the tower were bought from a nearby recycle centre.
He said the friends worked from morning until evening for three to four days to complete the structure.
The six-metre tower, designed to resemble the iconic structure, is also wrapped with Jalur Gemilang to add a patriotic touch in conjunction with the National Day celebration.
Another member of the group, Mohamad Asyraf Pakhrurazi, 30, said the project was also aimed at giving the village community something meaningful to enjoy together in conjunction with the 69th National Day celebration.
"We wanted to do something different this Merdeka. Seeing the tower standing in front of our houses has made everyone proud," he said.
The friends said they hoped their creation would attract visitors from nearby villages while spreading the spirit of patriotism and encouraging people to reuse discarded materials.
The replica has since become a talking point among residents, with many stopping by to take photographs with the homemade landmark.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Raja Muda of Perlis proposes three thrusts to guide Mara's future
Article:
KANGAR: The Raja Muda of Perlis Tuanku Syed Faizuddin Putra Jamalullail today proposed three main thrusts to guide Majlis Amanah Rakyat (Mara) personnel in steering the agency towards the future.
His Royal Highness said the first thrust was for Mara personnel to be bold in exploring and leveraging new technologies, particularly artificial intelligence (AI), to enhance efficiency, creativity and problem-solving capabilities.
"Mara should not merely adapt to change, but must be at the forefront of shaping the future," he said when officiating the 11th edition of Sukan MARA Se-Malaysia (Sukmas) at Dewan 2020 here today.
Also in attendance was Raja Puan Muda of Perlis Tuanku Dr Hajah Lailatul Shahreen Akashah Khalil.
Mara director-general Datuk Seri Zulfikri Osman was also present.
Tuanku Syed Faizuddin Putra said the second thrust was to continue strengthening the entrepreneurship agenda by producing innovative and resilient entrepreneurs who are bold enough to penetrate international markets, while building more local companies capable of competing and making their mark on the world stage.
He added that the third thrust was for Mara to produce personnel who were bold in leadership, quick to make decisions and strategic in their thinking.
He said future leaders should not merely follow change but emerge as catalysts and drivers of transformation.
Meanwhile, on Sukmas, he said the biennial tournament served as a platform to unite Mara personnel, strengthen ties, build discipline and foster the spirit of sportsmanship.
"By bringing together Mara personnel from various states, backgrounds and roles, sports become a common language that strengthens bonds and reinforces the spirit of togetherness as one Mara family," said His Royal Highness.
Meanwhile, speaking to reporters, Zulfikri said the 11th Sukmas was being held from today until Sept 3, featuring 15 sporting events including football, netball, volleyball, sepak takraw and tennis.
"It involves 3,000 athletes and officials from 14 Mara teams nationwide, and for us, this is a great opportunity for Mara personnel themselves to engage more closely with the community, particularly the people of Perlis," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Understanding, kindness key to strengthening national unity, says Loke
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: National unity begins with a conscious effort to understand one another, turning differences into sources of strength and enrichment rather than barriers, Transport Minister Anthony Loke Siew Fook said.
Speaking at the Merdeka Blessings Mahāsaṅghikadāna 2026 here today, he emphasised that Malaysia's diversity of ethnicities, religions, cultures and languages formed the foundation of the nation's strength, underpinned by mutual respect and care.
"True unity begins when we make the effort to understand one another. When there is understanding, differences no longer need to become barriers. They can instead become part of the richness and strength of our community," he said at the event.
Loke said diversity could only become an asset when accompanied by goodwill and respect among communities.
"Our diversity becomes a strength when it is accompanied by understanding. Our differences become a source of enrichment when they are accompanied by mutual respect. And our society becomes stronger when understanding is followed by kindness," he said.
Loke, who is also DAP secretary-general, said simple acts of goodwill could have a profound impact on social cohesion, whether through kind words that restored confidence, compassionate actions that eased burdens or generosity that bridged differences.
He said these values aligned directly with the core values of the Malaysia Madani framework, which strives to build a compassionate society founded on mutual trust and shared care.
With Malaysia set to celebrate its 69th National Day tomorrow, Loke said independence should be viewed not merely as an annual commemoration but as an ongoing commitment that must be upheld through everyday actions.
"As we celebrate our 69th Merdeka, we should remember that independence is not only something that we commemorate once a year.
"The strength of our nation must be renewed every day through the way we treat one another, through our willingness to understand those who are different from us, and through our commitment to place the well-being of our country above the differences that may exist among us," he said.
Loke said the gathering itself reflected its theme, "Understanding Unites, Kindness Blesses", by bringing together Buddhist monks, nuns and lay devotees from various traditions, including Thai, Sri Lankan, Burmese, Mahāyāna, Tibetan and Lao communities.
He said that despite differences in customs, languages and origins, the participants were united by a shared aspiration for the peace, harmony and prosperity of Malaysia.
Loke also expressed appreciation to the United Buddhist Order of Malaysia (UBOM), participating organisations, the Saṅgha and volunteers for organising the event.
"On this meaningful Merdeka occasion, let us continue building a Malaysia in which our diversity is not merely accepted, but understood, respected and cherished as one of our nation's greatest strengths," he said.
The 2026 edition is the first time the annual event has been held in Kuala Lumpur, following three consecutive years of gatherings in Penang.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Haze: Public urged to reduce outdoor activities in Sarawak
Article:
KUCHING: The public, particularly parents, have been urged to avoid outdoor physical activities during the school holidays to protect their children's health amid deteriorating air quality caused by transboundary haze.
Sarawak Deputy Minister for Urban Planning, Land Administration and Environment Datuk Len Talif Salleh said precautionary and early preventive measures should be taken, particularly by high-risk groups such as children, the elderly and people with chronic illnesses and respiratory problems.
"This advice is not only for children, but for all of us, especially now that the Air Pollutant Index (API) has reached 300 to 400, which is at hazardous levels. We advise everyone to be cautious and also wear masks, especially those in high-risk groups.
"We strongly advise high-risk groups and the elderly to take the necessary measures or adopt the best approach to safeguard their health by wearing masks and reducing outdoor activities," he told reporters here today.
The public was also urged to stay alert to official announcements and daily API readings, while ensuring exposure to air pollution was kept to a minimum throughout this critical period.
Len Talif, who is also Sarawak Natural Resources and Environment Board (NREB) deputy chairman, said the upward trend in API readings was caused by hotspots in Kalimantan, as well as dry weather conditions, which were expected to persist until the end of the year, putting Sarawak on alert.
"For the implementation of cloud seeding operations, as the state government announced previously, we will carry them out in early September. We are still assessing whether the process needs to be expedited by taking into account the current impact of the haze," he said.
Air quality in several areas in Sarawak deteriorated significantly, with Serian, Samarahan and Kuching recording hazardous API readings as of 12.30pm today.
According to the Department of Environment's (DOE) Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS) portal, the API reading at the Serian district police headquarters (IPD) monitoring station reached 412, followed by Samarahan (332) and Kuching (304).
Sri Aman, meanwhile, recorded a very unhealthy API reading of 228.
