Title: Venezuela says retains 'sovereignty' in US oil deal
Article:
CARACAS: Interim leader Delcy Rodriguez assured the public Saturday that Venezuela retains control of its oil under a new agreement that allows the United States significant access to it.
The United States will have majority control of 65 billion barrels of Venezuela's proven reserves in what President Donald Trump described Friday as "the biggest oil deal in world history".
"One thing must be absolutely clear: Venezuela retains ownership and sovereignty over its resources," Rodriguez said in a speech on state television.
The agreement with the United States aims to turn "cold, inert" resources underground to "a source of social and economic well-being for the people of Venezuela," she said.
Caracas says the deal involves $100 billion in private investment aimed at revitalising the industry in a country with the world's largest proven oil reserves.
But a lack of transparency is raising concerns among Venezuelans, including supporters of the government. A flood of social media comments decried loss of sovereignty, meagre benefits and political costs.
"We don't know who this will benefit – whether it's Venezuela or (the United States)," said Jesus Salazar, a 68-year-old security guard.
"I have my doubts, but we'll have to wait and see what happens."
Venezuela's government has operated under intense pressure from the Trump administration since American forces ousted and captured long-time ruler Nicolas Maduro in January.
Washington allowed Rodriguez, his vice president, to stay on as interim leader so long as she toes Washington's line.
Venezuela's ruling party said Saturday it supports economic measures that "prioritise national interests and make it possible to overcome the impact of more than a decade of economic sanctions, unilateral coercive measures, and unjust blockades."
The party consistently blames US sanctions for the collapse of Venezuela's economy.
- Petrol and poverty -
Rodriguez has pushed through reforms in Venezuela's mining and petroleum industries, opening once tightly controlled sectors to private capital and foreign investment.
Washington, for its part, has eased sanctions imposed on Venezuela's oil sector under the Maduro government.
Oil production rose by 29.8 per cent between January and July, reaching 1.2 million barrels per day – still well below the three million barrels per day produced a quarter of a century ago.
The US deal aims to restore production to those levels, but analysts agree it would take time.
"The increase in production won't be seen for at least three or four years," said engineer Oswaldo Felizzola, a professor at the Institute of Higher Studies in Administration (IESA) in Caracas.
He welcomed the United States acting as a "guarantor" for investments in Venezuela, which has failed to attract significant capital for more than a decade.
"Without this, these fields would not be developed over the next 10 or 15 years," because state-owned Petroleos de Venezuela (PDVSA) "does not have the financial resources to do so."
An initiative of this magnitude could accelerate long-awaited economic recovery in Venezuela, a country still reeling from the brutal 80 per cent contraction between 2014 and 2021 that plunged millions of Venezuelans into poverty.
Many survive on a monthly minimum wage equivalent toUS$0.16, plus government subsidies that can reach US$240 per month – still far short of the estimated US$730 needed to buy basic food necessities for a family of five.
- Doubt and optimism -
Carlos Baco, a 74-year-old government employee, hopes oil revenues will start flowing under the new deal but said he hasn't felt the effects of the increase in oil production over the past few months.
"Consumer goods and food are more expensive... the dollar is rising and prices are going up," he said. "It's impossible here."
Rodriguez has promised more than US$204 billion in tax revenue from the deal, without providing details.
For analyst Elias Ferrer of the Orinoco think tank, the investment is good news, even without specifics.
"It's undoubtedly better than before. Before, this oil wasn't being extracted; if no one extracts it, no one pays royalties, and no one profits from it," he said.
"If everything is done correctly... this will be a great opportunity for Venezuela to see its oil sector revived," said attorney Dolores Dobarro, Venezuela's former deputy minister of energy.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Drug offences primary hub driving systemic crime nationwide, says AADK
Article:
KOTA KINABALU: Drug offences have been identified as a primary hub driving systemic crime in the country, linking at least 28 other types of crime, including theft, housebreaking and violence.
National Anti-Drugs Agency (AADK) director-general Datuk Ruslin Jusoh said the findings were based on a research report by the Home Affairs Ministry's Data Science Centre through a network analysis of Section 15(1)(a) of the Dangerous Drugs Act 1952.
"This shows that failure to address the issue of drug abuse has the potential to cause a resurgence of other systemically linked crimes," he told Bernama.
He said national statistics on drug addicts and abusers recorded 123,139 people in 2021, before rising to 137,176 in 2022 and 145,526 in 2023.
He said the figure surged to 192,857 people in 2024 before recording a slight decline to 191,832 last year.
For Sabah, Ruslin said five-year records showed 6,377 people involved in drug abuse in 2021, 8,156 in 2022, 8,567 in 2023, 9,207 in 2024 and 8,665 last year.
"Although the number of addicts in Sabah dropped, amphetamine-type stimulants (ATS) or syabu still dominate the statistics, involving 8,524 people," he said.
He said that the figure far exceeded other drug categories, which recorded 73 people for other drugs, 50 for cannabis, 11 for opiates and seven for psychotropic pills.
"Changing trends and forms of drug abuse are increasingly difficult to detect, particularly with the rise of synthetic drugs and the emergence of new psychoactive substances (NPS) mixed into vape liquids, such as etomidate and synthetic cannabinoids," he said.
Ruslin said illicit substances found in physical products resembling everyday items, alongside societal stigma towards people in recovery, posed major challenges for AADK in Sabah.
Regarding the age profile in Sabah, he said youth aged 19 to 39 recorded the highest number at 5,638 people, or 65.06 per cent of the total, followed by those aged 40 to 59 (2,963) and adolescents aged 13 to 18 (64).
By gender, 8,172 people involved in drug abuse in the state were male, while 493 were female.
AADK has also identified several drug distribution and addiction hotspots, including Manggatal and Putatan in Kota Kinabalu, Merotai and Balung in Tawau, Rancangan Sungai Manila and Bukit Garam in Sandakan, Telipok in Tuaran and Kinarut in Papar.
Youth involvement has had a negative impact on family institutions and led to a drain on household income, with the cost of obtaining drug supplies estimated at between RM30 and RM100 daily.
To address the issue, AADK is focusing on community-based prevention strategies through the SKUAD 2 Roda Tour, which serves as a mobile ambassador programme spreading anti-drug messages to rural areas and estates.
Strategic cooperation is also coordinated through the Drug Eradication Action Council (MTMD), chaired by the Sabah Chief Minister, alongside the Drug-Free Aspiration Tour and the People's Empowerment Movement (Gegar).
At the educational institution level, various prevention programmes are being implemented, including the Student Potential Exploration Camp, Excellent Organisation Lead Teachers Seminar, Junior Squad and Family Seminar.
"These efforts are critical to ensure that the Sabah Maju Jaya aspirations are not tainted by the threat of drugs, which demands the empowerment of village heads and Village Development and Security Committees as the eyes and ears of the government," Ruslin said.
He added that as of August this year, 360 people were undergoing the Institutional Medical Treatment Programme (RPDI), while another 1,237 people were participating in the Community Medical Treatment Programme (RPDK).
Meanwhile, Chief Minister Datuk Seri Hajiji Noor said that the Sabah government firmly rejected attempts to make the state a transit route or target market for drug trafficking following the successful seizure by enforcement authorities of various types of drugs worth more than RM240 million under Ops Coleoptera and Ops Bayu 2.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: South Korea names veteran technocrat Lee Hyoung-il as new finance chief in cabinet reshuffle
Article:
SEOUL: South Korea unveiled a major cabinet reshuffle on Sunday, naming First Vice Finance Minister Lee Hyoung-il as the new deputy prime minister and minister of economy and finance.
The administration also tapped ruling Democratic Party lawmaker Kim Seung-won to lead the Ministry of Justice, and named Kang Shin-chul, former deputy commander of the South Korea-U.S. Combined Forces Command, as the new defense minister, presidential chief of staff Kang Hoon-sik said in a televised address.
The reshuffle of the cabinet comes as President Lee Jae Myung's administration seeks to revitalize its international policy momentum as it enters its second year, at a time when analysts are questioning the sustainability of his expansionary fiscal policies amid a rout in the local bond market.
Lee Hyoung-il, a career technocrat who has held the vice finance minister position since June last year, inherits an economy running hotter than expected and will be working with a central bank that is now tightening policy as the government is expected to boost fiscal spending for the year ahead.
The government is expected to roll out its 2027 budget next week.
In South Korea, cabinet nominees must face strict legislative scrutiny before they can formally be appointed by the president.
The president retains the ultimate constitutional authority to appoint his ministers, even if parliament votes them down.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Anwar pledges billions in seized funds for health, education; eases rules for small businesses
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Aug 30 — The government will channel billions of ringgit seized from illegal activities into public healthcare and education, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said today, leading a series of fiscal announcements he said were aimed at supporting low-income groups and small businesses.
Speaking during his National Day Eve address at the Putrajaya International Convention Centre here, Anwar said the move demonstrates the government's commitment to returning recovered proceeds of corruption and financial crime directly to the public.
"Today I declare that all funds seized from the proceeds of illegal activities through legal processes and decisions by the judiciary will be returned, especially for the people's education and healthcare," Anwar told the audience, including senior Cabinet ministers and top government officials who were also present.
As part of broader relief measures, Anwar also announced a new RM200 million grant scheme under the Geran Sejahtera Madani programme to assist hawkers, small traders, night market vendors, and mothers working from home.
The programme will take effect this coming Tuesday.
The government has also agreed to raise the mandatory e-invoicing exemption threshold from RM1 million to RM3 million in annual sales, as part of reliefs to help the small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs).
The new threshold was among the list of measures Anwar said would provide "temporary relief" as his government aims to alleviate living cost pressure and help businesses.
Earlier the prime minister announced the monthly quota for petrol and diesel subsidies would be reverted to 300 and 400 litres respectively, a decision he said was initially intended to be unveiled as a Budget 2027 initiative.

Title: Amirudin says Pakatan prepared for all scenarios, including solo Melaka fight if BN deal fails
Article:
GOMBAK, Aug 30 — Pakatan Harapan (PH) is always prepared for any eventuality in the Melaka state election, including contesting on its own should negotiations on cooperation with Barisan Nasional (BN) fail to reach an agreement.
PH election director Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari said, however, that sufficient room should be given to the party leadership to assess the best strategic options before any decision is finalised.
“There is still time, so let’s wait and see how things develop. I am not in a position to make the decision. So I have been asked to discuss it, and let’s discuss. But if there is no one to discuss with, what can we do? We just move forward,” he said when met by reporters after attending the National Aspirations with Youth (Nanba) for the Central Zone Series 2/2026 here today.
Amirudin, who is also Selangor Menteri Besar, said this when asked to comment on a previous statement by Melaka PKR state leadership council (MPN) acting chairman Adam Adli Abdul Halim, who hinted at the possibility of PH contesting on its own should negotiations on cooperation with BN fail to reach an agreement.
He said the country’s political landscape remained dynamic and flexible, allowing each party room to determine its own approach in facing the election.
“As a political party, elections are our main business, and we will participate through various methods that can be considered.
“The situation is now rather fluid, and everyone can determine their own way of gaining the people’s support,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Sarawak Rivers Board warns Rajang journeys perilous as haze blinds boatmen, drought shrinks channels
Article:
SIBU, Aug 30 — River transport users in Sarawak have been advised to plan their journeys carefully and exercise greater vigilance amid the current drought and haze conditions to avoid untoward incidents.
Sarawak Rivers Board (LSS) chairman Dr Safiee Ahmad said the drought had caused river levels to fall, making navigation channels shallower and narrower, while haze had reduced visibility.
“Conditions become more challenging when haze causes limited visibility, especially at night. I advise all river transport users to plan their journeys as best as possible and, if possible, avoid travelling at night.
“In addition, reduce the speed of your respective boats or vessels as visibility is impaired due to haze, as river water levels are also falling due to the drought and lack of rain in upstream areas. This measure is crucial to prevent danger to other river users,” he told Bernama today.
Safiee, who is also the Daro state assemblyman, said LSS continuously monitored river conditions and carried out enforcement through its enforcement divisions at regional offices throughout Sarawak.
He said river transport users could also obtain the latest information on river water levels and advisory services from regional LSS offices to help them plan safe journeys.
A Bernama survey yesterday afternoon and today found thick haze blanketing the Rajang River, Malaysia’s longest river, as well as the Igan River, after API readings rose to unhealthy levels. — Bernama

Title: Debt dispute sparks armed George Town school fight, police arrest 13 suspects including minors
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Aug 30 — Police have arrested 13 male suspects, including three minors, to assist in investigations into a violent brawl involving weapons that occurred in front of Sekolah Jenis Kebangsaan Cina (SJKC) Kong Min branch in Air Itam here early yesterday.
Penang police chief Datuk Dennis Lim said all the suspects, aged between 16 and 33, were arrested in five raids across the state through an operation conducted by the Criminal Investigation Department’s Vice, Gambling and Secret Societies Division (D7) of the Penang Police Headquarters, together with the Northeast District Police Headquarters Criminal Investigation Division and with assistance from the Central Police Station.
“All the suspects, including the three minors, were arrested under the joint operation, held from 8.19pm yesterday until 4.22am today, with those detained including a student, two unemployed individuals and several workers from the food delivery and transport sectors.
“Investigations are ongoing and the case is being probed under sections 148 and 326 of the Penal Code. The investigation papers will be completed before being referred to the Deputy Public Prosecutor for further instructions,” he said in a statement today.
He said investigations found that the incident occurred at about 2.45am yesterday, with the armed brawl involving two primary targets aged 17 and 25, adding that it was believed to have stemmed from a debt dispute following a meeting between several individuals at a food court in Kota Bali, Paya Terubong here.
Lim said police were also investigating a vehicle that allegedly struck one of the victims during the brawl, inflicting injuries.
He said that as a preventive measure, police would step up patrols and monitoring at high-risk locations, enhance intelligence gathering and conduct targeted operations to curb group fights and violent crimes.
“Those with information regarding the incident are urged to contact investigating officer Insp Nurul Izzati Rohim at 013-4092884 or the nearest police station,” he added, while urging the public not to speculate or circulate the identities of the minors involved.
He also advised the public against taking the law into their own hands or resorting to violence to settle disputes.
Lim added that police would also consider action under the Security Offences (Special Measures) Act 2012 (SOSMA) if investigations found the offences met the requirements for its application. — Bernama

Title: Deputy minister presses Wisma Putra for hotline, briefings as 91 Malaysians missing in Nepal‑China
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 30 — Wisma Putra has been urged to establish a dedicated one-stop centre to provide direct, regular and consistent updates to the next of kin of 91 Malaysians who remain uncontactable following the disaster at the Nepal-China border.
Deputy National Unity Minister R. Yuneswaran said the centre should be equipped with a 24-hour hotline, case reference numbers and officers who could be contacted at any time.
“A dedicated liaison officer must also be appointed for each family so that no next of kin is left out of the information loop and they do not have to contact various agencies to obtain updates,” he said in a statement today.
Based on a Wisma Putra statement as of 8pm yesterday, 55 Malaysians in Nepal and 36 in China remained uncontactable, with the figures still being verified and cross-checked to avoid duplicate reports.
Those uncontactable include tourists, climbers, pilgrims visiting Mount Kailash and two officers from the Malaysian Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM).
Yuneswaran also proposed daily briefings at fixed times for the affected families, even if there was no new information.
“A silence of information will only add to the stress and suffering of the families,” he said.
He said coordination between Wisma Putra, the National Disaster Management Agency (Nadma), JBPM, Nepalese and Chinese authorities, travel agencies and telecommunications companies must be intensified to verify travel manifests, passport numbers, travel routes and the last known locations of the individuals.
He also proposed that psychosocial support be provided to the families in collaboration with the Social Welfare Department and The Health Ministry, alongside assistance with documentation, travel and logistics for next of kin who need them.
He urged the public not to spread unverified information, photographs or figures, as this could cause confusion and heighten the families’ anxiety. — Bernama

Title: Budi95 quota restored to 300 litres, Anwar announces goodies ahead of Merdeka celebration
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Aug 30 — The monthly quota for petrol and diesel subsidies will be raised again, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim revealed today as he announced several goodies ahead of tomorrow’s Merdeka Day celebration.
Anwar suggested the move was initially intended to be unveiled as a Budget 2027 initiative, but he decided to announce it early as a means to provide “temporary relief”.
Currently the Budi95 programme sets the quota at 200 litres of subsidised RON95 a month. This will be raised back to 300 litres, effective 1 September 2026. For diesel, the quota would be raised from 300 to 400 litres a month. Anwar said the programme would benefit 16 million people.
The reversion to the original threshold is among a list of goodies the prime minister announced on the eve of Merdeka Day celebration here, where he delivered an official message that usually predates the National Day parade.
“It is hard but we must care for everyone. How do we ensure the T20 keep investing? How do we help the M40, the B40?” Anwar said, as he admitted to facing allegations that top and middle-income brackets often feel they are excluded from government programmes.
“With the M40, do we not give anything? I’d like to remind them that in 2023 we reduced income tax by 2 per cent. This led to the loss of RM1 billion in collection. Then there was the salary increment for civil servants. With school assistance, every family get it regardless of income background,” he added.
In his address, Anwar pointed to complaints that his government has not done enough, but suggested the accusations are ill-informed by highlighting all the major assistance that his leadership has provided up until now, including a staggering RM40 billion subsidy bill to keep petrol cheap even for high income earners.
“There is a tendency to complain about what the government has not yet done, but never to admit to God and be grateful for what we have received,” he said.
“I’ll give you an example, there is assistance that cost RM40 billion for all. What is that? Budi95.”
Anwar’s coalition secured the most seats at the 15th general election on the promise to alleviate cost of living pressure.
Despite strong growth numbers, among them a 6 per cent growth recorded in the April to June period, there is still grumbling that much of that prosperity is not trickling down, a point the prime minister acknowledged in his speech.
“Even in these tough times, we raised the SARA cash assistance, for example to RM15 billion, the highest in history. Is this the solution to all, no. Will this solve the living cost pressure, not yet,” he said.
“We admit that there are still steps to be taken.”

Title: Melaka’s Ab Rauf to steer BN–Pakatan talks, Zahid says timing depends on dissolution
Article:
SERDANG, Aug 30 — Barisan Nasional (BN) chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi says formal negotiations with Pakatan Harapan (PH) on possible cooperation for the Melaka state election will begin only after the state assembly is dissolved.
He confirmed the matter but explained that the talks would be led by Melaka BN under Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh, who has been tasked with negotiating and finalising any decisions,
Berita Harian
(BH) reported today.
The deputy prime minister, who is also Umno president, noted that only informal discussions between BN and PH have taken place so far.
He said Ab Rauf had already briefed the BN political bureau in Melaka, with details presented to the party’s supreme council for further study based on data compiled by its war room.
“We are handing this to Datuk Seri Ab Rauf, and I believe he will hold formal discussions once the Melaka assembly is dissolved,” Zahid told BH.
Separately, PH election director Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari said the coalition was waiting for Ab Rauf to indicate his readiness before negotiations could begin.
The PKR vice president, who is leading the talks, added that he had contacted Ab Rauf but was told to wait for a policy decision from BN and Umno’s central leadership.

Title: Three‑year‑old’s gold necklace snatched at Nilai food festival, police probe RM2,900 theft
Article:
NILAI, Aug 30 — A woman lost RM2,900 when her three‑year‑old daughter’s gold necklace was snatched while they were strolling at a food festival in N9 Arena here last night.
According to
Berita Harian
(BH), Nilai district police chief Superintendent Johari Yahya said the incident occurred at about 9.30pm when the girl told her mother her necklace was gone.
He said the 29‑year‑old woman lodged a police report at about 10.30pm, explaining that she had gone to the festival with her two children earlier that evening. While walking through the crowd, her three‑year‑old suddenly complained that her necklace had been pulled off.
Johari said the mother immediately checked and realised the gold chain was missing.
He told BH that the woman asked her daughter if she had seen or recognised the suspect, but the child only said it was a man.
Johari noted that the victim could not provide further details given her young age. The loss was estimated at RM2,900 and the case is being investigated under Section 392 of the Penal Code.

Title: Two relief centres opened after Kota Kinabalu fire tragedy leaves 200 victims homeless
Article:
KOTA KINABALU, Aug 30 — Two temporary relief centres have been opened at Dewan Kampung Likas and Dewan Damai to shelter more than 200 victims of a fire that broke out in Kampung Lok Buta, Numbak here early this morning.
Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Sabah and Sarawak) Datuk Mustapha Sakmud said the move was to facilitate the registration and coordination of all victims, as well as the distribution of donations.
He said the Kota Kinabalu City Hall (DBKK) had declared the area a disaster zone following the incident.
Speaking to reporters after visiting the area here today, Mustapha emphasised the need to identify the students affected to ensure that the fire did not disrupt their studies.
Joining Mustapha during the visit was DBKK mayor and District Disaster Management Committee chairman Datuk Seri Dr Sabin Samitah.
Mustapha, who is also the Sepanggar Member of Parliament, said he would inform the Ministry of Education of the situation to ensure that affected students from schools, higher education and Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) institutions received appropriate assistance.
He also urged DBKK and the relevant agencies to hold a meeting and discuss measures to assist those affected by the disaster.
“We will have a Malaysia Agreement 1963 (MA63) Implementation Action Council meeting, which will be attended by the Prime Minister (Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim) and the Chief Minister (Datuk Seri Hajiji Noor). Perhaps the DBKK mayor can brief both leaders on the situation and what needs to be done for fire-affected area,” he said.
Mustapha said he would also extend initial assistance to the families of the three victims who died in the incident at 1.40am today.
More than 200 houses were destroyed and three children, including two siblings, lost their lives in a fire in Kampung Lok Buta here early this morning.
Three children, including two siblings, were killed after a fire destroyed more than 200 houses in the village.
They victims were identified as Nana Abdullah, 4, her brother Mohd Asrul Abdullah, 6, and their cousin Nurfarahdilah Mohd Tajihah, 8. — Bernama

Title: Zahid: Cloud seeding targets haze‑hit areas and dams with falling water levels
Article:
SERDANG, Aug 30 — Cloud seeding operations are being carried out in haze-affected areas, particularly those recording Air Pollutant Index (API) readings above 150, as well as in areas where dams are experiencing falling water levels.
Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said the operations were being carried out in collaboration with the Malaysian Meteorological Department (METMalaysia) and the Royal Malaysian Air Force (RMAF).
He said the measure was necessary to prevent disruptions to water supply amid the current hot weather.
“This needs to be done because we know that water levels at many dams have been declining. Cloud seeding is being carried out in Putrajaya today, and will be conducted in Sarawak, Kedah and Perlis from Sept 3 to 5.
“Cloud seeding is carried out not only according to need but also depending on weather conditions. Even when clouds are present, we need to monitor their movement to determine whether they are moving towards the targeted areas,” he told reporters after launching the Laman Usahawan Desa KKDW at the 2026 Malaysia Agriculture, Horticulture and Agrotourism Show (MAHA) here today.
Three areas in Sarawak recorded hazardous API readings as at 12.30pm today.
According to the Department of Environment’s (DOE) Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS) portal, the API reading at the Serian Police headquarters monitoring station reached 412, followed by Samarahan at 332 and Kuching at 304.
Sri Aman, meanwhile, recorded a very unhealthy API reading of 228. — Bernama

Title: PM: Malaysia sends SMART team to locate missing citizens in Nepal, commits US$1m aid
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 30 — The Madani Government has decided to deploy the Special Malaysian Disaster Assistance and Rescue Team (SMART) to Nepal to assist in search and rescue (SAR) operations following the devastating floods in the country.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the National Security Council (MKN) and the National Disaster Management Agency (NADMA), in collaboration with the Foreign Ministry, have been tasked with coordinating with the Nepalese government to facilitate the deployment of the team as soon as possible.
“The SMART team has also been tasked with locating and bringing home Malaysians affected by the disaster, as well as assisting the Malaysian Embassy in Nepal in coordinating aid and ensuring their safety and welfare,” he said in a statement today.
Anwar said Malaysia would also contribute US$1 million (RM4.03 million) to Nepal to assist those affected and support post-disaster recovery efforts.
Yesterday, Foreign Ministry confirmed that 55 Malaysians remain uncontactable following the severe flash floods and landslides that struck Rasuwa district, Nepal, on August 26. — Bernama
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the National Security Council and the National Disaster Management Agency, in collaboration with the Foreign Ministry, have been tasked with coordinating with the Nepalese government to facilitate the deployment of the team as soon as possible. — Picture via Facebook/Anwar Ibrahim

Title: DOE: Transboundary haze thickens 1,211 hotspots detected in southern Asean, mostly in Kalimantan
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 30 — Some 1,211 hotspots were detected across the southern Asean region based on National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) satellite imagery analysed by the Asean Specialised Meteorological Centre (ASMC) in Singapore yesterday.
Department of Environment (DOE) deputy director-general (Development) Azuri Azizah Saedon said 1,180 hotspots were detected in Kalimantan, 18 in Sumatra and 13 in Malaysia, comprising two in Perak, two in Sabah and nine in Sarawak.
She said the Regional Haze Map issued by ASMC on the same date showed dry conditions prevailing across most of the southern Asean region, except for several areas, particularly northern Sumatra and Peninsular Malaysia, which received rainfall.
“Widespread hotspots were detected in Kalimantan, while isolated hotspots were recorded in Sulawesi and southern and central Sumatra. Several hotspots were also detected mainly in central Sarawak and eastern Java,” she said in a statement today.
Moderate to thick transboundary haze was detected over West Kalimantan, moving northwards into western Sarawak. Moderate to thick haze was also observed across much of Kalimantan, central Sarawak, and central and southern Sumatra.
Azuri Azizah said several air quality monitoring stations in West Kalimantan, western and central Sarawak, western Peninsular Malaysia, and southern and central Sumatra recorded unhealthy to hazardous air quality levels.
However, she said the overall extent of hotspots and haze in the region could not be fully determined due to cloud cover.
Following an increase in hotspot activity and the wider spread of haze in the southern Asean region, the Asean Secretariat activated Alert Level 3 for the region on Aug 27 in accordance with the  Standard Operating Procedures (SOP) for Asean Monitoring, Assessment, and Joint Emergency Response. (MAJER).
Meanwhile, the DOE continues to monitor air quality, hotspots, weather conditions and haze developments under the National Haze Action Plan (PTJK), while coordinating response measures with relevant ministries and agencies.
In Sarawak, the state DOE is continuing patrols and Open Burning Prevention Operations (OMPT), while stepping up monitoring in areas at risk of open burning, including forests, peatlands, landfills, agricultural and plantation areas, and industrial sites.
Under the PTJK, all outdoor activities must be suspended when the Air Pollutant Index (API) exceeds 100, while schools, kindergartens and nurseries must be closed immediately when the reading exceeds 200.
Schools, kindergartens and nurseries are also required to monitor API readings and prepare for possible closures if the trend shows an increase towards 200.
A DOE report at 9 am today showed that 13 areas recorded unhealthy API readings, two recorded very unhealthy levels and another two recorded hazardous levels. The highest reading of 374 was recorded at the Serian District Police Headquarters in Sarawak.
The public is advised against open burning and urged to report any burning or fire incidents to the Fire and Rescue Department at 999 or the DOE at 1-800-88-2727. — Bernama

Title: Haze worsens as Serian hits 412, while Samarahan and Kuching record hazardous API levels
Article:
KUCHING, Aug 30 — Serian, Samarahan and Kuching recorded hazardous-level Air Pollutant Index (API) readings as of 12.30pm today.
According to the Department of Environment (DOE)’s Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS) portal, the API reading at the Serian District Police Headquarters monitoring station stood at 412, followed by Samarahan (332) and Kuching (304).
Sri Aman, meanwhile, recorded a very unhealthy API reading of 228.
Areas recording unhealthy API readings include
Sarikei (197), Sibu (190), Bintulu (183), Mukah (176), Samalaju (175), Kapit (161), Miri (159) and the the Miri Industrial Training Institute (ILP) (156).
An API reading of zero to 50 indicates good air quality, 51 to 100 (moderate), 101 to 200 (unhealthy), 201 to 300 (very unhealthy) and above 300 (hazardous).
API figures are updated hourly based on readings from 68 monitoring stations nationwide. — Bernama

Title: Govt explores Melaka as alternative venue for LIMA, says Khaled Nordin
Article:
MELAKA, Aug 30 — The government is exploring the possibility of holding the Langkawi International Maritime and Aerospace Exhibition (LIMA) in Melaka in the future, said Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin.
He said, however, that substantial government investment would be needed to ensure the necessary infrastructure was adequately developed before the exhibition could be held in Melaka.
“Looking at Klebang, it is not far from Batu Berendam, which has an airport, and ships can also be berthed here. So, this is actually a location that could serve as an alternative to Langkawi.
“When LIMA is held in Langkawi, not many people are able to attend. But if it is held in Melaka, people from across the country could come. So, this is an alternative that we can explore, although as Datuk Rauf (Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh) said, it would require very substantial investment,” he said.
He spoke to reporters after launching the Civil-Military Cooperation Carnival (CIMIC) at Dataran 1Malaysia, Klebang, here today.
Earlier in his speech, Mohamed Khaled said the government planned to hold the biennial exhibition in Melaka if Langkawi was no longer deemed a suitable venue in the future.
He said the idea arose following the participation of six Royal Malaysian Navy (RMN) ships in this year’s Melaka-level National Day celebrations.
Ab Rauf said the state government was prepared to host the international exhibition, but would first need to assess its capacity and the benefits it would bring to Melaka.
“Melaka is indeed a strategic location for hosting LIMA, but we also need to consider our capacity.
“This matter can be discussed at the federal government level later. If it truly benefits both the federal government and the state, then why not go ahead with it, God willing,” he said.
Meanwhile, the Defence Ministry’s Strategic Communications Unit said in a statement that CIMIC, being held from Aug 29 to 31, serves as a platform to strengthen civil-military cooperation while giving the public an opportunity to learn more about the Malaysian Armed Forces (MAF). — Bernama

Title: Fatimah orders agencies to ensure welfare support for family in Sibu child death
Article:
SIBU, Aug 30 — Sarawak Women, Children and Community Wellbeing Minister Datuk Seri Fatimah Abdullah will instruct the Social Welfare Department (JKM) and Early Childhood Development Division (BPAK) to closely monitor developments in the case of a boy who is believed to have been slashed to death here last Friday.
She said this was to ensure that the family affected by the tragedy received appropriate welfare support and psychosocial assistance.
“I am deeply saddened and shocked by the tragic incident that resulted in the death of a child in Sibu.
“My condolences go out to the victim’s family. No child should ever be a victim of violence under any circumstances. The loss of a child is a deeply painful tragedy for any family,” she said in a statement today.
Fatimah said she was informed that police investigations were underway and that a suspect had been remanded to assist in the investigation.
Therefore, she urged all parties to allow police to conduct a thorough and transparent investigation without interference.
Fatimah also urged the public not to spread unconfirmed information, pictures or speculation, which could add to the grief of the victim’s family and potentially interfere with the investigation.
“For now, let us pray that the victim’s family and all those affected by this heartbreaking tragedy will be given strength and perseverance,” she said.
A five-year-old boy died after he was believed to have been slashed in an incident at a house in Jalan Rantau Panjang Jaya here last Friday.
Sibu district police chief ACP Abang Zainal Abidin Abang Ahmad said a man in his late 40s had been remanded for six days until September 4, and the case was being investigated under Section 302 of the Penal Code. — Bernama

Title: Melaka PKR plans early candidate announcements, Adam Adli says new faces need preparation
Article:
MELAKA, Aug 30 — Parti Keadilan Rakyat (PKR) Melaka plans to announce its candidates for the upcoming state election earlier to give its new faces sufficient time to be fully prepared before facing voters.
Acting chairman of the Melaka PKR Leadership Council Adam Adli Abdul Halim said the candidate selection process is undergoing several stages of screening, starting at the branch and state levels, before being submitted to the central level to be finalised by the party president.
“We have a history, where several times previously and due to various factors, we had difficulty announcing the names of candidates early. So, this time, we have made sure that we can prepare early because we are trying to field many new faces.
“This is also to ensure there is a balance of voices between women and young people. Due to these factors, we have to prepare the candidates well in advance,” he told reporters after the launch of the Keadilan Election Machinery for the Hang Tuah Jaya branch in Taman Bukit Piatu here last night.
He said the Melaka PKR would also strengthen its election machinery through a series of launches in Tangga Batu, Hang Tuah Jaya, Alor Gajah, Masjid Tanah and Jasin.
Adam Adli, who is also the Deputy Minister of Higher Education, said its priority now was to ensure the party had a strong election machinery ready to get cracking, regardless of who was eventually selected as a candidate.
“Before we name any candidate, the most important thing is for us to ensure we have a solid machinery, one that works for the party and ready to support any candidate we field in the upcoming election,” he said.
Commenting on cooperation talks between Pakatan Harapan (PH) and Barisan Nasional (BN), he said informal discussions between the political parties had been held, but formal negotiations to finalise the form of cooperation had yet to be held.
According to Adam Adli, communication between parties was not only important to discuss the possibility of cooperation, but also to ensure the election is contested in a healthier manner and to avoid a culture of harsh and dirty politics.
He said PH and BN, however, had expressed their willingness to hold discussions, with PH election director Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari having contacted Melaka Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusof to find a suitable time for a meeting.
Adam Adli said PH also had its own preparations for the Melaka state election and did not rule out the possibility of going it alone if negotiations with BN fail to reach an agreement. — Bernama

Title: Senator says RCI vital to clarify Tabung Haji losses, systemic flaws demand scrutiny
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 30 — The Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) was crucial to determine whether Lembaga Tabung Haji’s (TH) investment losses stemmed from weaknesses in investment decision-making or other factors, said Senator Muhammad Hasbi Muda.
He said while losses were a normal part of investment activities and did not necessarily indicate criminal wrongdoing, the issues involving TH warranted a comprehensive examination given the number of troubled investments highlighted.
Speaking on a recent talk show produced by a local television station, alongside economist Professor Emeritus Dr Barjoyai Bardai, the senator said half of the 14 investments proposed for forensic audits had suffered 100 per cent losses, while TH’s financial position between 2014 and 2018 had also seen its liabilities exceed assets.
“We can determine from the findings whether the losses were due to weaknesses in the investment panel or whether something else was wrong.
“If the wrongdoing was straightforward, like someone stealing from a mosque collection box, we do not need an RCI. But in the case of Tabung Haji, it was systemic. The misconduct or misappropriation was difficult to determine through the usual methods. That was why we need the RCI,” he said.
Muhammad Hasbi said the term “sakau”, which refers to the unauthorised taking of money or property for personal gain, should not be viewed solely in that context.
He said it could also include improperly obtained benefits such as appointments, promotions or other gains, as well as offences including false claims and abuse of power.
Meanwhile, Barjoyai said weaknesses in procedures, governance and internal controls were among the issues that needed scrutiny when assessing TH’s past problems.
He said one area of concern was the way investments were valued, which he claimed was carried out by TH’s management and board of directors rather than through objective assessments by independent professionals.
The Malaysia University of Science and Technology (MUST) lecturer said investment impairment issues had occurred since 2014 and were flagged by auditor PricewaterhouseCoopers (PwC), but were not reported, even after warnings had been issued.
“Every valuation involved discretion because there was no absolutely precise value. But if they were conducted objectively by an independent team, it could have been better. This reflects institutional weaknesses in procedures, governance and internal controls,” he said.
Barjoyai said TH should therefore reassess its investment management capabilities as part of reforms to prevent similar weaknesses from recurring.
He said if TH wanted to focus on managing pilgrims and haj affairs, its investment management function could be entrusted to other investment institutions such as the Employees Provident Fund (EPF) or Permodalan Nasional Bhd (PNB).
However, he said if TH chose to continue managing its investments itself, major changes would be needed to ensure it had robust governance, procedures and professional valuation methods.
The 252-page RCI report was made public on July 29 and debated during a special sitting of the Dewan Rakyat on Aug 11. — Bernama

Title: Malaysia King expresses hope for smooth National Day celebrations after audience with PM Anwar
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 30 — His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, has expressed hope that tomorrow’s National Day celebrations will run smoothly, with all parties involved doing their utmost to ensure their success.
According to a post on Sultan Ibrahim Sultan Iskandar’s Facebook page today, His Majesty said this after granting an audience to Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim at Istana Bukit Tunku here.
"I hope the National Day celebrations will run smoothly, and I look forward to seeing everyone involved giving their best to commemorate this important event in our nation’s history,” said His Majesty.
During the meeting, His Majesty was also briefed on the latest developments in the country, including preparations for the celebrations.
The 69th National Day celebrations, themed ‘Malaysia Madani: Kesejahteraan Dinikmati’, are scheduled to begin at 8am tomorrow at Dataran Putrajaya, featuring 10,819 parade participants from 76 contingents and 22 marching bands.
Sultan Ibrahim and Her Majesty Raja Zarith Sofiah, Queen of Malaysia, are scheduled to attend the celebrations, along with Anwar and members of the Cabinet. — Bernama

Title: Three Malaysians among 261 foreign nationals unaccounted for after Gyirong mudslide at China‑Nepal border
Article:
GYIRONG (China), Aug 30 — Three Malaysians are among 261 foreign nationals from 23 countries identified as unaccounted for following a mudslide that struck Gyirong Port along the China-Nepal border in southwest China’s Xizang Autonomous Region on Aug 26, local authorities said Sunday.
The latest figure was announced at a press conference held by the regional government’s information office following a joint search and cross-checking of information by foreign affairs, public security, culture and tourism, and emergency management authorities, Xinhua reported.
The 261 foreign nationals include 104 from Nepal, 49 from India, 33 from Latvia, 18 from the United States, 15 from Britain, six each from Canada and Australia, four from South Africa, and three each from Malaysia, Germany and Russia.
Others unaccounted for include two each from Ireland, Estonia, France, the Netherlands and New Zealand, and one each from Kazakhstan, Finland, Lithuania, Portugal, Ukraine, Spain and Hungary.
Chinese authorities have notified the countries' embassies and consulates in China, according to the press conference.
Following multiple rounds of searches, site inspections and checks of individuals at the port, no foreign tourists are currently stranded in Gyirong County, the authorities said.
China has also opened two 24-hour English-language hotlines for the families of the unaccounted-for foreign nationals: 0086-891-6817165 and 0086-18308026705. — Bernama-Xinhua

Title: Police probe viral video of headscarves with incomplete Jalur Gemilang patterns in Subang Jaya
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 30 — Police are investigating a video clip that has gone viral depicting the sale of headscarves, allegedly featuring incomplete Jalur Gemilang patterns, at a supermarket in Subang Jaya, Selangor.
Subang Jaya police chief ACP Wan Azlan Wan Mamat said they received a report regarding the matter at about 4.49pm yesterday.
“Initial investigations found that only some of the headscarves had incomplete Jalur Gemilang patterns, which the supermarket received from a supplier.
“The supermarket had taken immediate action by removing and separating the headscarves identified as having incomplete Jalur Gemilang patterns from the sales area to prevent them from being sold,” he said in a statement today.
Wan Azlan said that following the circulation of the video, police were conducting investigations under. Section 5 of the Emblems and Names (Prevention of Improper Use) Act 1963 regarding the use of the Jalur Gemilang that did not comply with the prescribed specifications.
He said investigations were also being carried out under Section 504 of the Penal Code for intentionally insulting with intent to provoke a breach of the peace.
“The public is advised not to speculate about the matter that has gone viral on social media and to let the police conduct their investigation,” he said, while urging witnesses to channel information to the Subang Jaya District Police Headquarters at 03-7862 7100. — Bernama

Title: Three children killed as massive Kota Kinabalu fire razes over 200 squatter houses
Article:
KOTA KINABALU, Aug 30 — Three children were killed in a fire that swept through more than 200 houses in three villages here early this morning.
The Sabah Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) said in a statement that the victims were identified as Nana Abdullah, four; Mohd Asrul Abdullah, six; and Nurfarahdilah Mohd Tajihah, eight.
“The actual number of houses involved and the status of the victims are still being verified. Updates will be provided from time to time,” it said.
According to JBPM, the fire involved non-permanent stilt houses in a squatter settlement across three villages, namely Kampung Lok Buta, Kampung Lok Poring and Kampung Sabang Lama.
Firefighters managed to contain the blaze, preventing it from spreading to nearby areas, while overhaul operations continue.
A total of 39 personnel from the Kota Kinabalu, Lintas and Penampang Fire and Rescue Stations were deployed to the scene to conduct the firefighting operations. — Bernama

Title: Police confirm drowning after Kenyir boat hits tree stump, victim trapped beneath overturned vessel
Article:
KUALA BERANG, Aug 30 — An elderly woman died after the boat she was travelling in hit a tree stump before capsizing around Gua Bewah, Tasik Kenyir in Hulu Terengganu yesterday.
Hulu Terengganu police chief Supt Sharudin Abdul Wahab said initial investigations found that the victim, who was from Felda Chiku in Kelantan, had come to Tasik Kenyir for a holiday on a houseboat with 27 family members.
“At 11am yesterday, the victim, 63-year-old Wan Esah Wan Daud and three other family members boarded a houseboat from Tasik Kenyir heading towards Taman Negara. When they reached the location of the incident at about 4pm, they all disembarked from the houseboat, which was parked at Gua Bewah, to go sightseeing by boat before it hit a tree stump.
“The collision caused the victim to fall into the water and become trapped underneath the overturned boat. She was rescued by other family members and taken to the houseboat,” he said in a statement today.
Sharudin said the victim’s son tried to perform cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) on her, but since there were no positive signs, the victim was taken in a boat belonging to the Department of Wildlife and National Parks (Perhilitan) for about an hour before reaching the mainland at Tasik Kenyir.
“The victim, who had a history of lung disease, was confirmed dead due to drowning,” he said, while advising the public to always prioritise safety when engaging in recreational activities, especially in lakes and rivers. — Bernama

Title: Farres Putra dies after Cub Prix crash, Kuala Terengganu police confirm multiple injuries
Article:
KUALA TERENGGANU, Aug 30 — A post-mortem has confirmed that multiple injuries sustained in a crash during the Malaysian Cub Prix Championship were the cause of death of CKJ Racing rider Farres Putra Mohd Fadhill, 18, yesterday.
Kuala Terengganu police chief ACP Azli Mohd Noor said the post-mortem was conducted at the Forensic Department of Sultanah Nur Zahirah Hospital (HSNZ) from 10pm to 11.55pm yesterday.
He said the crash occurred during the CP150 final race of the fifth round of the championship at the Gong Badak Motorsport Circuit and involved three motorcycles that collided with each other.
Farres, who was from Selangor, was taken to the HSNZ Emergency Department by ambulance and was pronounced dead by a medical officer, he said in a statement today.
Meanwhile, Farres’ friend Adi Putra Anahar, 17, said he was in a car watching the race live on his smartphone when the broadcast suddenly ended.
Adi Putra, who represents the Honda KC Racing Team, said the last time they met was last Thursday afternoon while they were on their way back to their homestay in the Gong Badak area.
“Yesterday, I took the opportunity to watch the live race from the car as my racing session had already ended. I was puzzled when the broadcast suddenly ended.
“Not long after that, I received a call from a friend informing me that Farres had been involved in an accident. I rushed to the hospital, but was told that he had passed away,” he said when met at the HSNZ Forensic Department last night.
Adi Putra, also from Selangor, said Farres’ death had deeply affected him as they had been close friends since they were 13.
“We have been friends for a long time because we were both involved in motorsports. We would hang out together two or three times a week.
“I am aware of the risks involved in motorsports, but I never expected to lose him in the blink of an eye,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Nepal floods leave 55 Malaysians uncontactable, 36 more missing in China, says ministry
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 30 — A total of 91 Malaysians, comprising 55 in Nepal and 36 in China, remain reported as uncontactable as of 8pm on Saturday following the floods that struck on Aug 26, the Foreign Ministry said.
In a statement, the ministry said it will continue to work closely with the relevant Chinese and Nepalese authorities while cross-checking figures from both countries to rule out duplicate reporting.
It also urged members of the media and the public to refer to the figures issued by the ministry when reporting on Malaysians affected by the situation in Nepal and China, as the figures may change when contact is established with Malaysians concerned and further reports are received from the relevant authorities and families.
“The Ministry understands the heightened concern regarding the limited personal information released publicly on individual Malaysians who remain uncontactable,” it said on Saturday.
It added that, in accordance with established consular procedures, information on individual cases is provided directly to verified immediate next of kin.
Consular officers have contacted all verified immediate next of kin whose details are available to provide updates on current developments.
It said personal details will not be released publicly without the consent of the immediate next of kin.
“While the Ministry appreciates the concern shown by friends, relatives and members of the wider public, the interests and welfare of the Malaysians currently reported as uncontactable, as well as those of their immediate families, remain the Ministry’s utmost priority.
“The Ministry therefore urges all parties to respect the privacy of the affected families and to rely on official information as consular efforts continue,” the statement read.
The ministry urged immediate next of kin who have yet to provide their details to contact the Ministry’s Operations Room, which operates 24-hours a day, to assist Malaysians affected by the situation and their families at +603 8887 4570 (telephone) or email dutyofficer@kln.gov.my.
Family members may also provide relevant details to the Embassy of Malaysia in Kathmandu (mwkathmandu@kln.gov.my) or the Embassy of Malaysia in Beijing (mwbeijing@kln.gov.my), with a copy to the Ministry’s Operations Room. — Bernama

Title: Foreign minister says briefing today for families of Malaysians missing in Nepal floods
Article:
SEREMBAN, Aug 30 — A briefing will be held today with the families of Malaysians still unaccounted for following severe flash floods and landslides in Nepal’s Rasuwa district.
Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan said the briefing will involve Wisma Putra, the National Security Council and relevant agencies to provide an update on efforts to locate those reported missing.
He said Wisma Putra is ready to arrange for the families to travel to Nepal if necessary, adding that access to the disaster area remains difficult due to damaged infrastructure, including bridges that have been severed.
“Many people who were initially reported missing have since been contacted. The Chinese authorities have also told us that several people there have been reached, but their nationality has not yet been confirmed,” he told reporters after the Ziarah Kasih programme at Taman Kelab Tuanku, Mamba, here yesterday.
Mohamad said the ministry’s operations room is operating round the clock to monitor developments involving Malaysians affected by the disaster, with Wisma Putra maintaining close communication with Nepal’s Foreign Ministry and relevant agencies for updates.
He said additional staff had been deployed to the Malaysian Embassy in Kathmandu to help handle the needs of Malaysians and their families who remain unaccounted for. — Bernama

Title: Serian tops hazardous API chart at 364, multiple Sarawak districts suffer worsening air
Article:
KUCHING, Aug 30 — Serian recorded a hazardous Air Pollutant Index (API) reading as of 8am today.
According to the Department of Environment (DOE)’s Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS) portal, the API reading at the Serian District Police Headquarters monitoring station stood at 364.
Meanwhile, three areas in Sarawak recorded very unhealthy API readings, namely Samarahan (300), Kuching (291) and Sri Aman (214).
Areas recording unhealthy API readings include Sarikei (195), Sibu (187), Bintulu (179), Samalaju (171), Mukah (170), Kapit (159), Miri (155) and the Miri Industrial Training Institute (ILP) (151).
An API reading of zero to 50 indicates good air quality, 51 to 100 (moderate), 101 to 200 (unhealthy), 201 to 300 (very unhealthy), and above 300 (hazardous).
API figures are updated hourly based on readings from 68 monitoring stations nationwide.
Meanwhile, five areas in the peninsula, namely Kuala Lumpur, Selangor and Perak recorded unhealthy API readings as of 9am today.
According to the APIMS portal, Batu Muda in Kuala Lumpur and Johan Setia in Selangor recorded API readings of 153 each, followed by Tanjung Malim (121) and Taiping (113) in Perak, and Cheras, Kuala Lumpur (105).
Bernama reported yesterday that asthma cases in the country had surged amid worsening air quality caused by haze affecting several areas nationwide, with 1,811 cases recorded in Epidemiological Week (EW) 34 (Aug 23-29), compared with 219 cases in the previous week.
The Health Ministry (MOH) said the figures were based on surveillance data from sentinel facilities.
The ministry said conjunctivitis cases also rose to 720 from 146 in EW 33, while upper respiratory tract infection (URTI) cases fell by 50 per cent to 1,857 from 3,674.
It said no deaths linked to complications arising from the haze had been reported.
Following the rise in respiratory-related illnesses, the MOH advised the public, particularly high-risk groups such as children, senior citizens and those with chronic lung conditions, to limit outdoor physical activities and wear suitable masks, such as N95 masks, when outdoors. — Bernama

Title: Early morning fire in Kota Kinabalu squatter area, 39 personnel deployed to contain blaze
Article:
KOTA KINABALU, Aug 30 — A fire broke out at stilt houses in a squatter area in Kampung Numbak here early this morning, with the number of houses involved yet to be confirmed as firefighters continue to battle the blaze.
The Sabah Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM), in a statement, said it received an emergency call at 1.40am, following which firefighters were deployed and arrived at the scene, located 18 kilometres away, at 1.58am.
“A total of 39 personnel from the Kota Kinabalu, Lintas and Penampang Fire and Rescue Stations (BBP) were deployed to the scene to carry out firefighting operations,” it said.
According to the Sabah JBPM, firefighters were battling the blaze using two streams and four water jets, with water supplied by fire engines.
Efforts to extinguish the fire are still ongoing, and further information on the incident will be provided from time to time.
No information on victims has been received so far, with the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) and other relevant agencies also assisting in the firefighting operations. — Bernama

Title: Beyond monuments and textbooks, KL’s Statesman Memorial guards Malaysia’s nation‑building story
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 30 — As Malaysia turns 69, the country has witnessed its fair share of history — from the struggle for independence and the formation of the federation to almost seven decades of nation-building, political change and rapid development.
Yet much of that history lives on not only in records and textbooks, but also in the places where key decisions were made and in the stories of those who helped shape the country through its formative years.
One such place is the Statesman Memorial (also known as Memorial Negarawan), housed in the former Prime Minister’s Office (PMO) along Jalan Dato Onn, which bears witness to the country’s post-independence administrative history.
Built in 1957 along what was then known as Brockman Road, the Brutalist-inspired building was built to replace Tunku Abdul Rahman’s
Old Office Building
nearby, and later served for decades as the seat of the federal government and the workplace of Malaysia’s prime ministers.
National Archives of Malaysia (ANM) director-general Zaidin Mohd Noor said the building’s historical significance lies not merely in its role as an administrative office, but as a physical witness to Malaysia’s journey in governance and development.
“One lesser-known aspect of the building is that it was more than just the PMO; it was also an important setting for government deliberations and decision-making in post-independence Malaysia.
“During its years of operation, various government policies, development plans, security issues, international relations and decisions that significantly impacted the lives of Malaysians were discussed and implemented there,” he told
Malay Mail
during a recent interview.
ANM director-general Zaidin Mohd Noor speaks to Malay Mail during an interview. — Picture by Yusof Isa
The former Prime Minister’s Office housed the tenures of Tun Abdul Razak Hussein, Tun Hussein Onn and Tun Dr Mahathir Mohamad — who occupied the office for the longest period, 22 years — until the federal government administrative centre moved to Putrajaya in 2003.
While museums and historical galleries typically bring collections and artefacts into exhibition spaces, Zaidin said the Statesman Memorial instead takes visitors to an actual site directly connected to the country’s administrative history, offering them a distinctly different experience.
Beyond its administrative role, Zaidin said the building itself was also a setting for significant moments in Malaysia’s diplomatic history, hosting notable foreign figures in 1990, including Nelson Mandela, then deputy president of the African National Congress, and Yasser Arafat, chairman of the Palestine Liberation Organisation.
“What makes the Statesman Memorial particularly distinctive is the building’s authenticity.
“Rather than being purpose-built as a new exhibition space, the memorial occupies a historic building that once served as a centre of government administration,” he said.
Where history lives
Beyond displaying documents, photographs, collections and materials related to the nation’s statesmen, the Statesman Memorial also retains elements and spaces linked to the building’s original function.
Key preserved spaces include the former Prime Minister’s Office and the Cabinet meeting room, which remain largely intact with their original setup.
The meeting room where Cabinet meetings were held every Wednesday, with Dr Mahathir presiding over the final meeting there on June 16, 1999. — Picture by Yusof Isa
Another notable exhibit is the original setup of the Baling Talks, held at Baling English School as depicted in history books, where negotiations between the Malayan government and communist representatives attempted to resolve the Malayan Emergency after World War II.
This in turn allows visitors not only to see history, but also in some instances, to experience the very spaces where it unfolded.
For younger generations, experiencing these spaces first-hand could deepen their appreciation of Malaysia’s development and foster a stronger sense of history, identity and civic responsibility, Zaidin added.
“In heritage preservation, authenticity is one of the most important values. As such, preserving spaces such as the PMO and Cabinet meeting room carries significance beyond simply retaining a room or its furniture layout.
“The arrangement of tables, chairs, documents, equipment and other elements within the room can help visitors envision how the country’s leaders carried out their duties, deliberated and made decisions while fulfilling their responsibilities.
“The spaces also symbolise the continuity of Malaysia’s governing institutions, preserving not just the physical rooms but the memories and meaning embedded within them,” he said.
The old Prime Minister’s Office was first occupied by Abdul Razak on Sept 22, 1970, and remained in use until Dr Mahathir vacated it on Oct 31, 2003. — Picture by Yusof Isa
More importantly, Zaidin said a country’s history is not always shaped by major events witnessed by the public, but also through the deliberations and decisions made behind closed doors.
“Ultimately, the building stands as a physical witness to nation-building, where national leaders made decisions that shaped Malaysia’s policies and direction.
“Therefore, its historical value lies not only in who occupied it, but also in the many affairs of state that took place within its walls,” he said.
Following the federal government’s move to Putrajaya, the former PMO received a facelift nearly a decade later in 2012 and was developed into what it is today after the Cabinet approved the memorial’s establishment at the site with RM30 million in funding under the 10th Malaysia Plan.
Seven figures, shared legacy
In actuality, the memorial chronicles the contributions of seven statesmen from Peninsular Malaysia, Sabah and Sarawak — Tun Dr Ismail Abdul Rahman, Tun Tan Cheng Lock, Tun VT Sambanthan, Tun Dr Lim Chong Eu, Tun Datu Mustapha Datu Harun, Tun Fuad Stephens and Tun Jugah Barieng.
“The seven were chosen for their significant contributions to the country, including their roles in the struggle for independence, shaping key national policies, community development and strengthening national unity.
“The inclusion of figures from Sabah and Sarawak also recognises their roles in the formation of Malaysia in 1963, reflecting the country’s history as a federation built on cooperation across regions and communities,” Zaidin said.
An office setup of former deputy prime minister Tun Dr Ismail Abdul Rahman, including personal items at the Statesman Memorial. — Picture by Yusof Isa
In each statesman’s gallery, exhibits include correspondence, photographs, personal collections and official records, offering visitors a glimpse into their thoughts, principles and leadership values.
While the statesmen are often remembered for their nation-building roles, Zaidin said there are many lesser-known stories and fascinating facts featured at the memorial that may be unfamiliar to the public.
“For example, Tan’s collection includes documents from around 1946 and 1954 that offer insights into political debates of the time, including the Malayan Union, democracy, elections and voting rights, helping visitors understand the challenges and ideas that shaped the country before independence.
“What makes the stories of the seven statesmen particularly compelling is their diverse backgrounds, yet their contributions complemented one another in building the nation.
“Their stories show that Malaysia’s development was not the work of a single leader or community, but the result of the struggles, cooperation, courage and commitment of many,” he said.
Personal items on display at former MIC president Tun VT Sambanthan’s gallery at the Statesman Memorial. — Picture by Yusof Isa
Although preserving the entire building is part of ANM’s responsibility to safeguard the country’s physical heritage and administrative memory, Zaidin said the Statesman Memorial ultimately goes beyond being a place to learn about the seven statesmen.
“It brings together the figures, documents, building and historic spaces to offer an authentic experience of Malaysia’s past, giving the memorial distinctive historical and educational value, particularly for younger generations,” he said.

Title: As cyber threats strike at AI speed, Malaysia urged to embed risk‑based defence
Article:
CYBERJAYA, Aug 29 — In the nearly 30 years since Malaysia began developing its national cyber emergency response capabilities with the establishment of MyCERT, the most significant change has been not merely the growing volume of cyber threats, but the speed at which attacks can occur, now further accelerated by artificial intelligence (AI).
Telekom Malaysia Chief Information Security Officer Raja Azrina Raja Othman, who was among the co-founders of MyCERT in 1997, said cyber threats three decades ago were largely confined to specific systems and networks.
Today, however, almost all services operate digitally and are interconnected, ranging from banking and government services to corporate operations and national critical infrastructure.
“When a cyberattack occurs, the impact goes beyond mere system downtime. It can compromise operations, finances, customer data and reputation, as well as disrupt services relied upon by the public,” she said in a special interview held in conjunction with the recent launch of TM’s 80th-anniversary celebrations, officiated by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.
She added that another major shift was the sheer speed at which cyberattacks could now be launched, with AI further accelerating the process.
“With AI, cyber attackers can more easily identify vulnerabilities, craft more convincing phishing campaigns and launch attacks at a much faster pace.
“Cyber attackers today operate rapidly with the aid of AI. Therefore, cyber defence strategies can no longer rely solely on manual processes,” she said.
Raja Azrina said the real challenge lies in increasingly complex information infrastructures driven by extensive application integration.
A lack of alignment between IT planning and information security could increase an organisation’s exposure to cyber threats, she said.
However, she observed that some organisations still viewed cybersecurity as an optional measure rather than an essential component of their operations.
“In reality, cybersecurity is a matter of risk management and business continuity. If core systems are compromised, can the organisation continue to operate? Can we maintain service delivery to customers? And will they retain confidence in our business?
“These are the questions organisations must address,” she added.
Therefore, she said, responsibility for cybersecurity must start with leadership and be embedded within organisational governance.
She stressed that cybersecurity investments should be guided by a risk-based approach, with organisations prioritising risks according to their potential impact on business operations.
“Even with cybersecurity investments, we cannot assume that attacks can be prevented entirely. Instead, we must be prepared for the possibility that an incident could still occur.
“What distinguishes truly prepared organisations is their ability to detect threats early, respond swiftly and remediate issues without causing prolonged disruption to operations.
“In cybersecurity, we cannot wait until a crisis strikes before deciding who needs to take action,” she said.
Raja Azrina said cybersecurity was not a new field for TM, as it had long been part of the company’s responsibility to manage and protect the nation’s digital infrastructure.
“TM’s cybersecurity capabilities are built on years of experience in protecting our own operations and supporting the digital needs of enterprises and the government, covering networks, cloud services, data centres and applications,” she said.
“Our teams continuously monitor security, drawing on their experience in managing vast and complex digital environments,” she added.
She noted that TM also had local cybersecurity experts specialising in various areas, including threat detection and monitoring, incident response and digital forensics.
“Based on our experience, cybersecurity monitoring and controls are required at every level - network, infrastructure and application - to establish layered protection and enhance the effectiveness of detection and response,” she said.
For Raja Azrina, the question today is no longer whether organisations will adopt AI, but whether they can do so securely while maintaining the trust of customers and the public, as security measures must evolve as rapidly as technology.
She said this was one of the key reasons TM developed the TM Cyber Defence Centre (TM CYDEC).
Through a “Cyber Fusion” approach, TM CYDEC enables comprehensive monitoring of cybersecurity issues across network, infrastructure and application security for the industry and government sectors. TM also has an AI security framework in place to govern AI security.
“We believe that the right cybersecurity strategy, a risk-based approach, and effective services and technologies can help organisations detect and respond to cyber threats earlier, thereby minimising their impact on business.
“Ultimately, our goal is to enable organisations to continue innovating and leveraging AI with confidence, without compromising security and trust,” she said. — Bernama

Title: Immigration to seek Thai details on syndicate trafficking China nationals from Cambodia into Malaysia
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 29 — The Immigration Department will work with Thai authorities to obtain detailed information on an alleged syndicate trafficking China nationals from Cambodia to Malaysia.
Immigration director-general Datuk Zakaria Shaaban said they were monitoring developments of the case even though they have yet to receive any official report on such activities.
“We will get further information from Thai authorities on this matter,” he said when contacted by Bernama today, after Thai media outlets reported that Thai authorities arrested two individuals suspected of being masterminds of a ring trafficking China nationals from the Cambodian border to Malaysia through Thailand.
Thai authorities found six China nationals and a Myanmar national who were waiting to be smuggled into Malaysia to work in a scam syndicate during a raid on a resort in Na Mom district in Songkhla province.
Thai authorities also identified four Thai nationals believed to be involved in the ring, including the individual arranging the immigrants’ journey from the Cambodia-Thai border to Hat Yai and onwards through to Malaysia. — Bernama
